strategy: Aberrant spectres can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 60 Slayer and level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They can be found in the Stronghold Slayer Cave, the second floor of the Slayer Tower, and in Deepfin Mine.

A nose peg or Slayer helmet is required when fighting aberrant spectres. Without either of those equipped, they will use a special attack which hits through protection prayers and drain the player's stats very quickly.

Aberrant spectres have a normal magic attack that has a max hit of 8. Protect from Magic will completely neutralize it. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Superior variation, the Abhorrent spectre may spawn. The Abhorrent has a max hit of 33, and Protect from Magic will still prevent its normal damage.
summary: Aberrant spectres use a magic attack with a max hit of 8 that Protect from Magic fully negates, but without a nose peg or Slayer helmet they use a special attack that hits through prayer and drains stats fast. They are undead, so a Salve amulet (ei) beats the Slayer helmet bonus, and they drop lots of herbs and seeds so a herb sack and seed box are recommended. The Stronghold Slayer Cave is the usual choice because a cannon can be used there, Nieve or Steve is right outside and a bank is close; the Slayer Tower gives bonus Slayer XP from the Morytania Diary. Deviant spectres in the Catacombs count too but have much higher defence and give lower XP rates.

strategy: At level 85 Slayer and Combat level, the player may be assigned Abyssal demons by mid and high levelled Slayer Masters and Krystilia. They can be found in the Abyssal Area, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Wilderness Slayer Cave, and in the Slayer Tower, where they are found on the third floor and in the task-only basement.

Abyssal demons use a fairly accurate melee stab attack, but with a relatively low max hit of 8. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Greater abyssal demon has a chance to spawn as a Superior slayer monster. The greater abyssal demon is much more powerful and accurate with a max hit of 27. Protect from Melee will neutralise all damage taken from either variation.
Players on abyssal demon tasks may also opt to kill the Abyssal Sire boss instead, which can be very profitable as compensation for significantly lower experience rates compared to Abyssal demons.

The Wilderness Slayer Cave is the only location in which a Cannon can be used against Abyssal demons, although as part of the Wilderness, it is also a Player killing hotspot. The Wilderness Slayer Cave also allows taking advantage of cheaper Blighted supplies and the passive effects of the Accursed sceptre (a) and other weapons charged with Revenant ether.

With their 1x1 size, Abyssal demons are ideal for use with area of effect weapons including the Venator bow and Ancient Magicks. The Catacombs and Wilderness Slayer Cave are the only two Multicombat areas with Abyssal demons. As Abyssal demons are not aggressive, a method to cause them to attack the player, such as Dinh's bulwark or a Goading potion, is recommended.

Because of the teleportation mechanic, Smoke Barrage or Smoke Burst are favoured over their Ice equivalents. After teleporting away, frozen abyssal demons will not move back toward the player until they're unfrozen. Blood spells are significantly more expensive than Smoke and are not recommended.

Killing Abyssal demons outside multicombat areas, usually done only on a Konar task, will result in a slower task requiring more attention. If required to kill Abyssal demons in a single combat zone, it's recommended to use an Expeditious bracelet with a melee setup.

If the player is comfortable with the risk, Abyssal demons in the Wilderness Slayer Cave will provide some of the best rates of Slayer experience in the game. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are still an outstanding source of experience.

In single-combat areas such as the Slayer Tower a melee setup with an Expeditious bracelet is recommended. Extend this task as early as possible.

strategy: The Abyssal Sire is an abyssal demon Slayer boss that requires level 85 Slayer to kill. To access the boss, the player must have visited the Abyss at least once, either through the Mage of Zamorak or the Fairy Ring network. As with all other Slayer bosses, the Sire can only be fought when assigned abyssal demons (outside of Krystilia) or itself as a Slayer task. Although it resides in a multi-combat area, it is a solo-only boss.

According to The Overseer, the Abyssal Sires are the engineers of the Abyss from a time before the God Wars. As their resources began to deplete and they had no means to escape, they constructed the Nexus and remained there in deep stasis.

It is known for dropping the unsired, which can be placed in the Font of Consumption behind The Overseer for a chance of obtaining an abyssal whip, abyssal dagger, abyssal head, jar of miasma, a part of the abyssal bludgeon - the axon, claw, or spine - or, rarely, an abyssal orphan.

strategy: The Alchemical Hydra is a boss version of hydra, found in the lower level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon in Mount Karuulm, requiring level 95 Slayer to kill. The Alchemical Hydra was the creation of a Dragonkin named Karuulm. While Karuulm saw promise in his creation, he nevertheless saw it as a failure because he could not replicate its traits, and abandoned it along with his other creations: the Wyrms, Drakes, and Hydras.

Unlike normal hydras, the Alchemical Hydra can only be killed while on a hydra Slayer task, which are only assigned by Konar and Mortimer. Likewise, it can be assigned for boss slayer, but only by Konar.

In addition, as it is found within the volcano, players who have not completed the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary must wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots to protect themselves from the extreme heat of the dungeon floor. This also applies to attempting to use the Item Retrieval Service, where the rapid damage will interrupt actions and dying a second time will wipe the storage.

strategy: Ankou can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 combat by various Slayer masters. They can be found in the Sepulcher of Death, Stronghold Slayer Cave, the Catacombs of Kourend, and Deepfin Mine, as well as in the Wilderness in both the Wilderness Slayer Cave and the The Forgotten Cemetery. There are five variations of normal Ankou ranging from level 75 to 98. An additional variation, Dark Ankou, only appear when fighting the boss Skotizo, but they spawn infrequently and are almost always ignored in order to kill the boss faster. Damaged Dark Ankou that automatically die after Skotizo is killed will not count for a Slayer task.
Ankou attack with a relatively inaccurate melee attack that has a max hit from 8 to 10. Protect from Melee can be used to negate all damage.

Ankou are undead, therefore the Salve amulet and its variations can give a bonus to the player's accuracy and damage. The bonuses of the Salve amulet do not stack with the bonuses given by the Slayer helmet or Black mask. It is advised to check a Dps calculator with the player's current stats and other gear to determine if the Slayer helmet or the Salve amulet should be used.
summary: Ankou use an inaccurate melee attack with a max hit of 8-10 that Protect from Melee fully negates. They are undead, so a Salve amulet works (but not stacked with the Slayer helmet), and they are aggressive. Unextended tasks are fast with melee even in single combat; in the multi-combat Catacombs of Kourend or Wilderness Slayer Cave they can be bursted or barraged, and a cannon works everywhere except the Catacombs. The Stronghold Slayer Cave is the convenient default (cannon, task-only, near Nieve).

strategy: Aquanites are Slayer monsters found in the Ynysdail Cavern beneath Ynysdail. They require level 78 Slayer to fight, and accessing Ynysdail itself requires 73 Sailing and a boat equipped with an adamant keel or better.

Aquanites can be killed normally and Mortimer can assign them as a Slayer task by default; however, to receive them as a Slayer task from Nieve or Duradel, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. A task extension is also available for 100 points.
Aquanites can drop the unique Aquanite tendon, used to make the Aquanite hopper.

Accessing Ynysdail requires the player to enter the crystalline maze from the outside, or build the rowboat hotspot on the island. This rowboat, once built, will generate another one north of Gwenith. Using this rowboat requires completion of Song of the Elves. It is recommended to complete the quest to avoid having to set the ship back to a mooring point if a greater teleport focus is not on it.
summary: Aquanites are accurate magic attackers found only in the Ynysdail Cavern, so Protect from Magic is strongly recommended; alternatively they can be safespotted with a 9-10 tile attack range. Hitting one with a slash attack severs its lure and drops its stab defence from 60 to 10, so the usual method is a fast slash weapon followed by a strong stab weapon. The cavern is single-way and a cannon cannot be placed. Reaching Ynysdail needs 73 Sailing and a boat with an adamant keel or better; building the rowboat there (70 Construction) gives a fast route from Gwenith after Song of the Elves.

strategy: Araxytes are a potential slayer assignment from Nieve/Steve, Duradel/Kuradal, and Mortimer, after completion of Priest in Peril. Turael/Aya and Spria can also assign them, albeit indirectly as a spiders task. They require 92 Slayer in order to be harmed and are found exclusively in the Morytania Spider Cave.

Araxytes attack with melee, and are also able to inflict venom starting at 6 damage, therefore, it is recommended to bring venom immunity to all encounters, preferably extended anti-venom+ for long trips. They are fairly far from a bank, though a spider cave teleport will bring players to the entrance of the cave.
summary: Araxytes are melee attackers in the Morytania Spider Cave that inflict venom, so bring venom immunity (extended anti-venom+ for long trips) and prayer. Kill only the level 146 variant: it has the better drop table and is the only one that can spawn the Dreadborn Araxyte superior. A cannon works throughout the cave and, combined with a Venator bow in the multi-combat rooms, kills them very quickly; barraging is possible if you stack the 2x2 larger araxytes by running through them. The task is very profitable so bring a seed box and herb sack; a spider cave teleport lands at the entrance.

monsters.name: Aviansie

requiredItems: Ranged or Magic weapon (or a halberd / salamander)
strategy: Aviansie can be assigned as a slayer task provided that players have access to the God Wars Dungeon (requiring completion of Death Plateau) and has unlocked Watch the birdie slayer perk for 80 Slayer reward points.

Aviansie can be found in the normal and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon; as followers of Armadyl, Armadylean God-aligned items are required to make them tolerant. Aviansie have an increased sense of danger and will attack players if they are attacked, even if they're in combat with another monster. Their flying height means that they can only be harmed with ranged and magic, although salamanders and halberds are an exception as a direct target.

Aviansie have a somewhat generous drop table that mostly revolves around adamantite bars, runite limbs, ensouled aviansie heads and poisoned rune daggers, the limbs and daggers having reasonable high alchemy price. Aviansies in the God Wars Dungeon will only drop the bars noted if the player has completed the Hard Fremennik Diary, whereas those in the Wilderness drop them noted regardless of diary completion. Though unlikely, it is possible to be killed by other players in the Wilderness, and its dangers force players to bring less than optimal gear if minimising risk.
styleNotes: Low Risk Melee: Ranged - Low Risk
summary: Aviansies fly, so they can only be hit with Ranged or Magic (halberds and salamanders are the melee exceptions), and they attack with Ranged. They are Armadylean followers: an Armadyl-aligned item makes them tolerant, but they will still turn on you the moment you attack one. The task must be unlocked with Watch the birdie (80 points) and needs God Wars Dungeon access; the God Wars Dungeon is the normal spot (multi, no cannon, Hard Fremennik Diary notes the adamant bars), while the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon (entrance at level 28 Wilderness) drops bars noted regardless of diary. Many players kill Kree'arra and his bodyguards instead, banking at Nex.

The level 22 guard bandits and level 130 bandits at the southern entrance are aggressive, so enter from the safer eastern entrance (guarded only by giant rats) and consider trapping five of the level 130s inside the pizza shop and general store houses. Guard Bandits, Speedy Keith, Donny the lad and Black Heather all count. A single level 130 bandit in the Wilderness Slayer Cave also counts but is not recommended.

requiredItems: Earmuffs or Slayer helmet
strategy: Banshees can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 Slayer and level 20 combat by various Slayer masters. They are found in the Slayer Tower and the Catacombs of Kourend. Players must wear earmuffs or a Slayer helm when fighting banshees. Lower levelled players who do not have access to a Slayer helm can wear a salve amulet. Note that the bonuses from the salve amulet do not stack with those from the Slayer helmet.
Banshees are primarily known for their common drops of pure essence, which is helpful for ironmen for runecrafting.

A stronger variant of banshee, the Twisted Banshee, can be found in the Catacombs of Kourend. These are often killed over normal banshees as they are still easy to kill (notably being safespottable) and have much better drops; battlestaves, rune equipment, and larger quantities of herbs.
summary: Banshees are a low-level task that requires earmuffs or a Slayer helmet, otherwise their scream deals damage and heavily drains stats. They are undead, so a Salve amulet works for players without a Slayer helmet. Normal banshees are on the ground floor of the Slayer Tower (single-way, safespot south of the stairs); Twisted Banshees in the Catacombs of Kourend are usually preferred because they are still easy, safespottable on the bridge between their rooms, and drop far better loot (battlestaves, rune items, herbs, pure essence). Neither location allows a cannon.

strategy: The Barrows brothers were a band of six legendary Saradominist warriors from a small town in Misthalin who ventured into Morytania during the God Wars, leading the Morytania Campaign. Their fate is revealed in the crumbling tome. They struck a deal with a mysterious stranger for power, and after their deaths, the Stranger came to 'collect' them, and they were buried in six burial mounds, or Barrows, in eastern Morytania, giving them their collective name. Even after their deaths, they remain as wights. Their names are in alphabetical order from the oldest brother (Ahrim), to the youngest (Verac).
They can be killed by players as part of the Barrows minigame.
Barrows brothers can be assigned as a boss Slayer task.
summary: The six Barrows brothers (Ahrim, Dharok, Guthan, Karil, Torag and Verac) are fought in their burial mounds at the Barrows east of Mort'ton and can be assigned as a boss Slayer task with no Slayer level requirement beyond Priest in Peril for Morytania access; only brother kills count, not chests.

strategy: Basilisks can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 Slayer, level 40 combat, and level 20 Defence by medium level Slayer Masters. The high level masters will not assign them until players unlock Basilocked using Slayer reward points. Ordinary basilisks, which can be found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon and Jormungand's Prison, attack only using an extremely inaccurate melee attack with a max hit of 5. Their thin drop table and high defence level generally make them worthwhile to skip, although their low weighting doesn't make them worth blocking.

However, after completion of The Fremennik Exiles quest, the player gains access to the Basilisk Knight in Jormungand's Prison, and basilisk tasks gain a new purpose for obtaining the powerful Neitiznot faceguard.
When fighting any basilisk, the player must equip a mirror shield or V's shield, or the basilisk's gaze will deal immense damage and massively drain the player's stats.
summary: Basilisks are fought with melee using crush weapons, and a mirror shield or V's shield must be equipped or their gaze deals immense damage and drains stats. Ordinary basilisks in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon only use a weak melee attack and can be safespotted, but their thin drop table and high Defence make them slow. After The Fremennik Exiles most players kill Basilisk Knights in Jormungand's Prison for the basilisk jaw; knights use melee and magic and can be safespotted from melee, praying against whichever style is reaching you. Cannons cannot be placed anywhere with basilisks.

strategy: Bears can be assigned as a slayer task at level 13 combat by various low-level Slayer masters. Bears can be found in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Black bears, bear cubs, grizzly bears, grizzly bear cubs, reanimated bears, Artio, and Callisto can all be killed to satisfy the task. Angry bears (found in Tolna's rift), the Headless Beast (fought during the quest Getting Ahead), and the Crystalline and Corrupted Bear (fought in the Gauntlet and the Corrupted Gauntlet respectively) do not count towards the task.

Those with lower combat levels would find it in their best interest to kill bear cubs, found in the Fremennik Province and throughout Kourend. Black bears would also be a good option, with a combat level of 19. Grizzly bears in most cases are an option if they are close, as most are level 21 combat. The only level 42 combat grizzly bears are found in Tirannwn. Grizzly bear cubs, too, can only be found in Tirannwn, with combat levels ranging from 33 to 36.
summary: A low-level task (13 combat) killed with any style; grizzly bears are the most widespread, black bears are non-aggressive and bear cubs are easiest for low levels. The cluster north-east of Ardougne and the woods outside Rellekka hold the most bears, and the four black bears outside the Mind Altar (between Ice Mountain and Goblin Village) are the biggest black bear group. Krystilia's assignment must be done in the Wilderness, where the bears west of the Graveyard of Shadows are the main option, or Callisto and Artio can be killed for their drops.

strategy: Black demons can be assigned as a Slayer task at 80 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of dungeons around Gielinor. Black demons can be easily killed using safespots when attacking with Ranged or Magic, or by using melee with the Protect from Melee prayer. They are weak to demonbane weapons, as well as water spells.

For lower-levelled players, black demon tasks can be very daunting, as their high stats requires safespotting, which will significantly lower kill rates. Higher-levelled players will not have this problem, but the demons have a near non-existent drop table which makes killing them generally not worth the time or experience.

The two best spots for killing black demons would be Taverley Dungeon or the Chasm of Fire. The former has many demons packed together while the latter has more safespots, and both are cannonable. The advantage of the latter is that those who have completed A Kingdom Divided and signed a contract with Yama will be able to get contracts from killing the demons. The drop rate is increased when killing them according to preference, but catering to this will prolong tasks and reduce AFK time. While black demons are also found in the Catacombs of Kourend, which is a multicombat area and have access to the catacombs table, it is generally not worth killing them there as they have unusually higher Defence compared to the other variants and it is not possible to utilise all four spawns.
summary: Black demons are killed either by safespotting with Ranged or Magic or by meleeing with Protect from Melee; demonbane weapons and water spells are strong against them. The two best spots are Taverley Dungeon, which packs 24 demons together, and the bottom level of the Chasm of Fire, which has more safespots; both are single-way but cannonable. Their drop table is nearly empty, so lower-levelled players who must safespot often skip the task. Demonic gorillas can be substituted (except on Krystilia or Konar tasks) and are profitable but slower.

trainingSummary.cons: Long task, especially if killing demonic gorillas. Using the cannon will result in a loss.
trainingSummary.pros: Decent experience rates, low-effort task. Demonic gorillas can be killed for good profit at the expense of experience rates.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Block/skip unless killing demonic gorillas for profit/uniques

strategy: Bloodvelds are a type of demon that use their long tongues to attack their victims. Being a Slayer monster, bloodvelds require a Slayer level of 50 to be damaged by players. As a demon, it is affected by demonbane weapons. An ash sanctifier may be brought to receive Prayer experience. Bloodvelds are popular among many players for their high Hitpoints and low Defence, thus making them good sources of experience.

Bloodvelds are one of few monsters that attack with magic-based melee, meaning that despite it using melee attacks against the player, it is the player's magic defence (rather than their melee defence) that is used to determine the accuracy of the bloodveld's attack. As such, it is recommended for players killing bloodvelds to equip armour with decent magic defence, such as dragonhide or blood moon armour, as they are relatively accurate in combat. Players using Prayer should still pray Protect from Melee instead of magic to nullify damage.

There are many locations to kill bloodvelds, though the most common one is the Stronghold Slayer Cave, due to its close proximity to a bank. The bloodvelds can also be killed here with a dwarf multicannon, requiring relatively low attention. The Meiyerditch Laboratories are notably multi-combat and cannonable. It is not recommended to kill bloodvelds elsewhere, as they take longer to access and/or are not cannonable. Bloodvelds have a superior variant, the insatiable bloodveld, if the perk Bigger and Badder is active.
summary: Bloodvelds have high Hitpoints and low Defence and attack with magic-based melee, so wear armour with good magic defence such as dragonhide and pray Protect from Melee if using prayer. The Meiyerditch Laboratories are the best spot because they are multicombat and cannonable with a cluster of seven mutated bloodvelds, giving the most experience per hour; the Stronghold Slayer Cave is the common choice for its bank proximity and cannon use. The God Wars Dungeon and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon locations are recommended to skip.

trainingSummary.cons: Travelling to the Meiyerditch Laboratories can take a while. Using a cannon will result in a loss in the Stronghold Slayer Cave.
trainingSummary.pros: Good experience rates when cannoning mutated bloodvelds in the Meiyerditch Laboratories or Buccaneers' Laboratory. Drops cover some of the cost of using the cannon if in Meiyerditch Laboratories.

strategy: Blue dragons can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 65 combat by mid- and high-level Slayer masters after starting Dragon Slayer I. They can be found in various caves across Gielinor, with most of them having some requirement to access, such as completion of quests, a dusty key, or level 70 Agility.

Blue dragons attack using melee, as well as dragonfire, for which some form of dragonfire protection should be considered. Additionally, brutal blue dragons can also attack with magic. Due to their large size, blue dragons can usually be safespotted with ranged, magic, or halberd-like weapons. Like all dragons, they are also susceptible to dragonbane weapons.

When assigned a general task of blue dragons, players who seek a fast task are recommended to bring a dwarf multicannon to Taverley Dungeon, using it against the baby blue dragons in the main dungeon, as the task-only area is full of adults. Players who want slightly more profit are recommended to kill the adult dragons. If players want the maximum profit from the task, it is highly recommended to complete Dragon Slayer II in order to access Vorkath, who has very consistent and valuable commons.
summary: Blue dragons use melee and short-range dragonfire, so bring an anti-dragon shield or antifire and pray Protect from Melee, or safespot them with Ranged, Magic or a halberd since they are large. For a fast task, take a dwarf multicannon to the main Taverley Dungeon and cannon the baby blue dragons; adults give more profit. Skip Konar tasks to the Ogre Enclave, Catacombs or Ruins of Tapoyauik (no cannon or spread-out dragons); Vorkath after Dragon Slayer II is the most profitable alternative.

strategy: Brine rats are Slayer monsters that can be found in the Brine Rat Cavern near Rellekka. They are notable for being the only monsters to drop the brine sabre. A Slayer level of 47 is required to fight them.

They are only assigned to players who have completed Olaf's Quest. Additionally, they can be killed as an alternative for a rat Slayer task provided the player has the appropriate Slayer level to do so.
Killing a brine rat is a requirement for completing the medium task set in the Fremennik Diary.
Brine rats have relatively low Defence, but fairly high Strength and Attack. As such, it is recommended to bring food if players do not have high (~70) Defence.

Players may instead opt to bring a number of Bones to Peaches tablets to convert their bones drops to peaches, which heal 8 hitpoints each. Bringing logs and a tinderbox to cook and eat the raw rat meat and occasional drops of raw swordfish and raw shark, may also be done, though this is significantly more time-consuming and less efficient than using peaches. Alternatively, Olaf, outside the caverns, has a permanent fire located beside him, so players may cook any unnoted food drops on his fire if they are willing to exit and re-enter the caverns. A fish barrel can be used to store the unnoted raw fish, though these drops are infrequent.

There are two safespots, one being the black bones to the south-east, and the other in the north-west corner of the cave. If the brine rats are in the north half of the cave, you are able to safespot them from behind the bones in the corner.
Click here for a picture guide of the safe spots.

Rat bone weapons can be used to kill brine rats and have an added 10 hitpoints of damage added to the player's max hit, making these weapons incredibly effective compared to other weapons with similar stats. Even compared to the highest tier weapons, rat bone weapons might still be more effective depending on your stats and boosts, as the difference in max hit based on other weapon's strength bonuses might not be enough to reach 10 hitpoints of extra damage towards their max hit.
summary: Brine rats live only in the Brine Rat Cavern near Rellekka, entered by digging with a spade south of the windswept tree (fairy ring DKS is right beside it). They have low Defence but fairly high Attack and Strength, so bring food unless your Defence is around 70; two safespots exist behind the bones in the south-east and north-west corners. Rat bone weapons add 10 to your max hit against them. The cavern is single-way but a cannon can be used.

strategy: Callisto is an enormous bear empowered by the corruption of the Wilderness that resides in Callisto's Den at level 40 Wilderness and is the one of two monsters to drop the tyrannical ring.
Ironmen are eligible for drops from Callisto when defeating it alongside other players.

In order to enter Callisto's lair, the player must have completed the medium Wilderness Diary tasks, OR they must have a Callisto boss Slayer task (a bear Slayer task does not bypass the diary requirement). Entering the boss lair requires players to pay a fee of 50,000 coins; this fee does not need to be brought along in the inventory, and can be deducted from the bank.

Callisto primarily attacks with melee, but will use ranged against players if he cannot reach them. His melee attack deals massive damage and shatters into other players near his current target. His melee attack has a minimum hit of 35.

If Callisto is not already frozen and the attacking player has equipment with a total Magic accuracy greater than 0, the first attack that would freeze the boss is guaranteed to hit and freeze Callisto.

At specific health intervals (66% and 33%), Callisto lifts his head, becomes unfrozen, and deploys bear traps that snare and damage players when stepped on. Callisto can be re-frozen after he returns to normal stance.

Callisto will occasionally send out a slow magic attack towards the player. If the player is not praying Protect from Magic when the attack reaches the player, this will result in the player being knocked back and temporarily stunned, in addition to taking a large amount of damage if the player is knocked into a wall.
Protection prayers will negate all ranged and magic damage of his attacks, but Protect from Melee will only reduce the damage by ~50%.
summary: Callisto is a level 470 bear boss in Callisto's Den at level 40 Wilderness, assigned as a boss task (Like a boss unlock) with Artio in Hunter's End as an accepted substitute.

strategy: Catablepon are magical creatures that appear to be green bulls with reptilian tails. They are found on the third level of the Stronghold of Security. They drop the top of sceptre, one of four parts of the Skull sceptre.
They have a weakening glare which drains your Strength, but will stop casting once 8% + 3 of your total strength level has been drained.

Players are not advised to train on these with Melee, as Weaken can drain Strength quite significantly, which will affect the player's experience rates in turn, unless Strength potions or Restore potions are used (you can also use the Protect from Magic prayer). They can use melee and magic attacks often and cast Weaken at the same time. After the spell has decreased 8% +3 of your Strength levels, catablepon will stop casting Weaken, but casts before this threshold can still bring you lower than the threshold. Ranged or Magic attacks are recommended instead of melee.

On the west side of north-western room, there is a ranged and mage safespot behind the "Stinking/Dripping tendrils" available. Walk into the western door and the westernmost tile behind the tendrils. Another safespot is in the same room. Enter from the western door and stand against the wall beside the door. Finally, another safespot is available in the room right before the central room. Standing in the north-westernmost corner of the room, it is possible to attack the catablepon from a distance. Level 64 catablepon give 70 Slayer experience per kill, while levels 68 and 49 give only 50 and 40 respectively, so to maximize for Slayer experience, only kill level 64 catablepon on task.
summary: Catablepon are found only on the third level of the Stronghold of Security, the Pit of Pestilence, and are assigned by Mazchna. They cast Weaken with their glare, draining Strength until 8% plus 3 levels are gone, so Ranged or Magic from the safespots behind the tendrils or doors in the north-western room is advised over melee, or use Protect from Magic and restore potions. They are aggressive and use both melee and magic. The level is single-way but a cannon can be set up in the stronghold.

strategy: Cave bugs are monsters that require level 7 Slayer to kill. They are found in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, requiring a light source and a rope to enter, and stronger variants can be located in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon. They are a good source of low level herbs, which can aid beginning players in training Herblore. Their Hitpoints regenerates once every 5 game ticks, 20 times faster than regular NPCs.

Cave bugs that are significantly more powerful—with a combat level of 96—can be found and safespotted in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, located south of the city of Dorgesh-Kaan, but can only be accessed after the completion of the Death to the Dorgeshuun quest through fairy ring fairy ring AJQ. After entering the dungeon and climbing down the ladder to the dungeon floor, level 96 cave bugs can be safespotted by standing in a passage between frogs and cave bugs (south-west of the ladder).
A light source is required for these dungeons, along with a rope to place down on the hole leading to the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, if it has not been done so previously.
summary: A beginner task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna at 7 Slayer. Level 6 cave bugs in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves die to any combat style and drop low-level herbs; the caves need a light source and a rope, and wall beasts in the corridors can grab you unless you wear a spiny helmet or run past them. Level 96 cave bugs in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon can be safespotted but need Death to the Dorgeshuun. Both variants regenerate hitpoints about 20 times faster than normal monsters.

strategy: Cave crawlers are Slayer monsters that require level 10 Slayer to kill. A form of poison protection is recommended when killing them, as they inflict a strong poison with their barbed tongue. They are the only enemy to drop bronze boots. They also drop a variety of Herblore ingredients, which can be helpful for lower level players looking for an alternative source of herbs over more popular sources, such as chaos druids. Lower level players should be aware that they have a rapid natural health regenerate rate, regenerating 1 hitpoint every 5 ticks.
If the Bigger and Badder Slayer reward has been unlocked, there is a chance that a Chasm Crawler will appear when killing cave crawlers on a Slayer task.

Players with very low Defence should use Ranged or Magic to attack these monsters in order to avoid being damaged and possibly poisoned, utilising the rocks around the room's walls in Fremennik Slayer Dungeon as safespots. You can use the fairy ring, fairy ring AJR, just outside as a fast means of banking.

When fighting cave crawlers in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, be aware that any exposed light sources (i.e candles) may explode, and can cause a considerable amount of damage. As such, a bullseye lantern or an oil lantern is recommended as it is not an exposed light source. You can use the Zanaris Shed to be teleported to Zanaris as a fast method for banking (either within Zanaris or to teleport elsewhere using the fairy ring itself).
summary: A low-level task at 10 Slayer usually done in the first chamber of the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, right beside fairy ring AJR. Cave crawlers hit up to 3 but inflict a strong poison, so bring antipoison; low-Defence players can range or mage them from the rocks around the chamber walls. They can also be killed in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves or Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, where a light source is needed and exposed light sources can explode. They regenerate 1 hitpoint every 5 ticks, so kill them quickly.

You must wear a witchwood icon to fight cave horrors at melee distance, otherwise they will use a special attack which always deals damage equal to 10% of the player's base Hitpoints level, rounded down (e.g. 9 damage at 96). This can be completely mitigated by using Protect from Melee, or using a safespot.
A light source is also required to fight them without taking additional damage, unless a fire of eternal light is lit.
summary: Cave horrors are found only in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave and need 58 Slayer, Cabin Fever, a light source and either a witchwood icon or Protect from Melee, because their scream always deals 10% of your base Hitpoints. They use magic-based melee, so most players either pray melee in prayer gear or use a fast Ranged weapon such as a toxic blowpipe from the many safespots near the cave entrance. A cannon can be used and there is a well-known cannon placement near the entrance where targeted horrors get stuck on the wall. They are killed mainly for the black mask and hard clue scrolls; bring a herb sack, seed box and log basket for the frequent herb, seed and mahogany log drops.

locations.name: Kraken Cove
locations.notes: 25 cave kraken whirlpools plus the Kraken boss room, which has a peek option to count players inside. Fairy ring AKQ lands just east of the cove; a Piscatoris teleport scroll or Western banner 3/4 also work. Lieve McCracken stops any attack made off-task.
requirements: Active Cave kraken or Kraken task

strategy: Cave kraken can be assigned from level 87 Slayer. They are exclusively found within Kraken Cove.

Cave krakens have low value drops and are generally only killed for their uncharged trident which has a 1/200 drop rate. The Noxious Halberd can reach them, however it will deal no damage. They also take reduced damage from ranged attacks, so they should be fought with Magic using earth spells due to their elemental weakness. Damage can be protected against with Protect from Magic.

Alternatively, the Kraken boss can be fought. Magic is also used, but Kraken's typeless attacks means that the damage cannot be prayed against. The fight is very simple and it has a fairly generous drop table. Fishing explosives are recommended to initiate the fight quickly, and can be easily obtained from any Slayer Master.
summary: Cave kraken live only in Kraken Cove and can only be attacked while on task; you must disturb a whirlpool to surface each one. Magic is the only reliable style because Ranged deals a seventh of its damage and melee cannot reach them, so use earth spells against their elemental weakness and Protect from Magic against their magic attacks. Their drops are poor apart from the uncharged trident, so most players kill the Kraken boss instead for the same task, using fishing explosives to start each fight quickly.

trainingSummary.cons: Poor experience rates. Killing cave krakens will result in a guaranteed loss due to the supplies needed to kill them with little net gain.
trainingSummary.pros: Decent and low-effort profit when killing the boss variant.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Block after achieving the kraken Combat Achievements

groups.text: Rope to enter the caves (only needed once)

locations.name: Lumbridge Swamp Caves
locations.notes: Slimes are in two rooms; open light sources ignite gas in the northern room but the entire southern room is risk free. You pass a wall beast to reach either room. Not aggressive.
requirements: Rope to enter the caves (only needed once)

locations.name: Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon
locations.notes: Nine spawns; reach via fairy ring AJQ. Antipoison recommended because several poisonous creatures live here.

requiredItems: Bullseye lantern (lit) or another enclosed light source (Fire of Eternal Light removes the need)
Rope (first visit to Lumbridge Swamp Caves)
strategy: Cave slimes are Slayer monsters that require level 17 Slayer to kill. They inflict poison regardless of whether they do damage or not, so it is advised that the player brings a form of anti-poison when fighting them. As they are located in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, a rope is needed if you have not entered the dungeon before. A light source is also required, but be aware that any exposed light sources (such as a candle) may explode, dealing up to 25% of the current Hitpoints level in damage if you go into the northern spawning room. A good option for an enclosed light source is an emerald or sapphire lantern. If a player is next to a cave slime when they attack they may be poisoned even if the slime does not retaliate.

Cave slimes are found in two rooms of the caves. Open light sources will flare brightly, and ignite gas in the northern room, however the entire southern room is risk free. For either room you will have to pass by a wall beast, so head protection (spiny helmet/Slayer helmet) can be helpful to avoid damage.
They have a guaranteed drop of roughly 3.5 swamp tar per kill, making them a decent low energy cost method for Ironmen to gather tar.
summary: A beginner task at 17 Slayer done in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves or the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon. Cave slimes hit only 2 but poison you even when they miss, so bring antipoison; any combat style works. In the Lumbridge Swamp Caves an enclosed light source such as a bullseye or sapphire lantern is important because open flames ignite gas in the northern slime room, while the southern room is risk free. Wall beasts guard the way to both rooms, so a spiny helmet or Slayer helmet helps.
usefulItems: Spiny helmet or Slayer helmet (wall beasts)

strategy: Cerberus is a level 318 hellhound boss who resides in Cerberus' Lair, deep beneath the Taverley Dungeon in the cave entrance in the north-east part of the hellhound area, which is found beyond the poisonous spiders. Defeating Cerberus requires a Slayer level of 91, along with a task of hellhounds or Cerberus herself. In the event of a hellhound or elite clue scroll task, wild pies may be used to boost the player's Slayer level. While boosting, the player's Slayer level must remain at or above 91.

Cerberus drops three different crystals: the eternal, pegasian, and primordial crystals which are used to upgrade the infinity, ranger, and dragon boots to the eternal, pegasian, and primordial boots respectively, which boast the second highest bonuses for the feet slot. She can also drop the smouldering stone at a much better rate compared to her lesser brethren, along with the jar of souls and the hellpuppy pet.
A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up inside Cerberus' Lair; if attempted, players will receive the message:
summary: Cerberus is a level 318 hellhound boss in Cerberus' Lair, entered from the north-east cave in the hellhound area of Taverley Dungeon, and needs 91 Slayer plus a hellhound or Cerberus task to fight.

locations.name: Chaos Temple (Wilderness)
locations.notes: 13 level 129 Elder Chaos druids around the altar, never tolerant, able to teleblock and pull you within melee range from 20 tiles unless you have read a teleport anchoring scroll. Burning amulet teleports to the north entrance in level 15 Wilderness; the altar restores prayer for Protect from Magic.

strategy: Chaos druids are low-level humans commonly killed for their frequent drops of herbs. Unlike other druids, they worship Zamorak. They attack with their fists and make use of a spell that appears to be a combination of the Confuse and Bind spells, binding their target very briefly if successful.

Players who decide to kill chaos druids in the Edgeville Dungeon should beware of player killers who disguise themselves in Zamorak robes to take on the appearance of a chaos druid. If you attack another player, you will become skulled and potentially lose all of your items.
summary: A Krystilia-only task, so only kills inside the Wilderness count. The usual spot is the level 1-5 Wilderness section of the Edgeville Dungeon, where 11 level 13 chaos druids die to anything and drop plenty of herbs. Elder Chaos druids at the Chaos Temple in level 11-13 Wilderness also count but teleblock, teleport you to them and hit hard with Magic, so use Protect from Magic there.

locations.notes: Deep multicombat Wilderness; bring only what you can afford to lose. Access via the deep Wilderness teleport lever in Ardougne or Edgeville, or a Wilderness obelisk (selectable after the hard Wilderness Diary).

strategy: The Chaos Elemental is a dark cloud with six tentacles that dwells in the members-only section of the Wilderness, just west of the Rogues' Castle. This area is moderately easy to access from the deep Wilderness teleport lever in Ardougne or Edgeville. The nearby Wilderness Obelisk can randomly teleport players south-east of the Rogues' Castle; after the hard Wilderness Diary is completed, the location can be chosen from any Wilderness obelisk.

The Chaos Elemental is generally killed for its dragon 2h sword and pickaxe drops. It also has a higher drop rate of the pet chaos elemental compared to the Chaos Fanatic. In addition, it is immune to venom—any items that are able to inflict venom will inflict regular poison instead.
- As this boss is located deep within the Wilderness, and wanders around in a multi-combat zone, beware of player-killers! Do not bring items you are not willing to lose.
summary: The Chaos Elemental is a level 305 boss wandering the multicombat Wilderness just west of the Rogues' Castle at about level 52-54, reachable from the deep Wilderness levers in Ardougne or Edgeville or a Wilderness obelisk, with no Slayer requirement.

strategy: The Chaos Fanatic is a relatively simple boss that resides west of the Lava Maze in level 42 Wilderness, surrounded by miniature chaotic clouds that serve as unattackable scenery. His special attack mechanic is similar to that of the crazy and deranged archaeologists.

The Chaos Fanatic is notable for dropping one of the three shards that form the malediction ward and odium ward, with the Crazy archaeologist and Scorpia dropping the other pieces. Killing all three at least once is a hard Wilderness Diary task.
He is one of the only monsters to drop the ancient staff, along with mummies, Calvar'ion, and the thermonuclear smoke devil.
summary: The Chaos Fanatic is a level 202 boss standing in single-way combat west of the Lava Maze in level 42 Wilderness, reached fastest by Ghorrock Teleport or a burning amulet to the Lava Maze, with no Slayer requirement.

requiredItems: Mirror shield or V's shield
strategy: Cockatrice are Slayer monsters that require level 25 Slayer to kill. A mirror shield or V's shield is required to defend against their piercing gaze, or else they will reduce your combat stats every hit, even while safespotting. As 20 Defence is needed to be able to wield a mirror shield, players who do not meet this requirement will not be assigned them as a task. It is worth noting that their strength lies purely in their piercing gaze ability; with a protective shield equipped, do not expect much of a fight. As such, not a lot of resources are necessary to hunt this monster.
They are rarely killed outside of Slayer tasks, generally only by those hunting the rare mystic boots (light) and cockatrice head drops.

A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Fremmenik Slayer Caves. Those looking to use a cannon should kill moonlight cockatrice instead (requires 48 Slayer to begin the Perilous Moons quest. For access to Neypotzli, only partial completion of the Perilous Moons quest is required)
summary: Cockatrice need 25 Slayer and a mirror shield or V's shield, otherwise their gaze drains your combat stats every hit even from a safespot; with the shield equipped they are a pushover and need few supplies. The standard task spot is the third chamber of the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (fairy ring AJR), which is single-file and cannot be cannoned. Players who want to cannon can kill Moonlight Cockatrice in Neypotzli instead, which requires partial completion of Perilous Moons.

strategy: Cows are common low level monsters new players train on. They are one of the first NPCs new players see outside of Lumbridge. Cows can help new players earn money, Cooking experience, and combat experience. The cowhides that they drop can be tanned to make leather or hard leather, or they can be sold for coins to players wanting to raise their Crafting level.

While most locations containing cows are crowded, there are some spots usually vacant, like the spot north of the windmill north-west of Lumbridge. Along with cows, you can also find cow calves and dairy cows. Regular cows cannot be milked; attempting to do so using a bucket will display the message.
summary: A level 2 beginner task from Turael and Spria that any combat style finishes quickly; cows hit a maximum of 1 and are not aggressive. The task list points to the pasture south of Falador and the field north of the Al Kharid gate east of Lumbridge, though cows are found in many farms and cow calves and undead cows also count. Cowhides can be kept for Crafting or sold.

strategy: Crabs can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters. They have no requirements to be assigned and are found in many areas across Gielinor. Crabs are often used as popular monsters for combat training, due to their low offence and high hitpoints. King Sand Crabs and Giant Rock Crabs are the exceptions, having much higher combat stats, and are only advisable to kill for a Slayer task if seeking specific drops from them (such as pieces of rock-shell armour).

As most crabs deal relatively little damage, no particular gear is required for them. Accounts with lower combat levels may need to wear armour or bring food, but at higher levels, neither are necessary. All crabs use the crush attack style, so if wearing armour, armour with the highest crush defence is advised. For example, a chainbody will offer more crush defence than a platebody.

All types of crabs initially appear as unattackable "rocks", but will emerge when a player stands in a neighboring tile. They will be aggressive, automatically attacking the player, but will become tolerant after 10 minutes have passed, and will no longer emerge. As they must be active to fight, the player must reset the crabs' aggression timer by leaving their immediate area and then returning.
summary: Crabs have no requirements and are the classic AFK training monsters: they sit disguised as rocks, emerge and attack when you stand beside them, and the common training crabs hit only 1 with crush, so no special gear is needed beyond crush-heavy armour at low levels. They go tolerant after 10 minutes, so you must walk away and come back to reset aggression. Sand crabs on the Hosidius coast and ammonite crabs on Fossil Island are the usual choices, but they cannot be targeted by a cannon; rock crabs north of Rellekka can be cannoned in multicombat. King Sand Crabs give the most Slayer XP but fight back, and Gemstone and hermit crabs do not count.
usefulItems: Food or armour with high crush defence at low combat levels
Dwarf multicannon (rock crabs and king sand crabs only)
Ring of wealth (auto-collects numulite from ammonite crabs)

requirements: Darkness of Hallowvale (the laboratories are entered during the quest); Sins of the Father for full access

strategy: Crawling Hands are Slayer monsters that require level 5 Slayer to kill. The Crawling hands are the first Slayer monster a player can defeat upon reaching the required level. They are also one of the creatures that will sometimes "die" in a perfect form allowing you to get it stuffed by a taxidermist and mounted in your player-owned house.
Due to their undead status, the Crumble Undead spell and the salve amulet do work on them.

While on a Slayer task with Bigger and Badder unlocked, there is a 1/200 chance that the crushing hand superior monster will spawn after a crawling hand kill. After claiming the elite tier rewards from the Combat Achievements system, this chance is increased to 1/150.
summary: A level 5 Slayer beginner task from Turael, Spria, Mazchna and Mortimer. Crawling hands are tiny undead with a max hit of 1-2, so any combat style with no prayer kills them; they are not aggressive and drop bones plus cheap gloves and rings. The usual place is the ground floor of the Slayer Tower north-west of Canifis, which holds 24 spawns, though the Meiyerditch Laboratories also have them. Because they are undead, Crumble Undead and the salve amulet work on them.

strategy: Bellock, the crazy archaeologist, is a relatively simple boss that resides in the ruins south of The Forgotten Cemetery within level 23 Wilderness. His special attack mechanic is similar to that of the Deranged archaeologist and the Chaos Fanatic.

The crazy archaeologist is notable for dropping one of the three shards that form the malediction ward and odium ward, with the Chaos Fanatic and Scorpia dropping the other pieces. Killing all three at least once is a hard Wilderness Diary task.
He is also a popular source for the rune crossbow, particularly amongst low to mid-level ironmen.
summary: Boss task for Bellock, the crazy archaeologist, who lives in the Western Ruins south of the Forgotten Cemetery in level 23 Wilderness; the deranged archaeologist on Fossil Island may be killed instead unless Krystilia or Konar specified the Wilderness.

locations.name: Along the River Elid
locations.notes: Stand on the south side of the river directly south of the small island where crocodiles spawn so they come to you. A cactus safespot lies directly west of the Nardah magic carpet. Bring waterskins; Nardah has a fountain and altar.

locations.name: Near the Ruins of Unkah
locations.notes: 'Players may also use the wall East of the Ruins of Unkah to safespot the crocodiles, negating the need for food and waterskins (as there are plenty of cacti to refill them from).'

locations.name: Near the Ruins of Ullek
locations.notes: 'The area south of the Ruins of Ullek, south-west of the teak trees has 12 crocodile spawns and does not require water for the player to survive, so long as the player stays in the grassy area near the water.'

strategy: Crocodiles are found in the Kharidian Desert south of Pollnivneach on either side of the River Elid. They are often assigned as Slayer tasks by Vannaka. Their drop table is rather poor, with only common herbs as a very rare drop, so you'll be getting only bones most of the time. Bring waterskins to avoid dying of thirst.

A great place to fight crocodiles is on the south side of the river, directly south of the small island where the crocodiles spawn. Because crocodiles are aggressive from a few squares away, this place attracts crocodiles from in the water where they cannot usually be reached, and is much less click-intensive. There is a safespot for crocodiles directly west of the magic carpet at Nardah, on a cactus near the river north-west of the crack in the desert. There are two crocodile spawns that can be safespotted, which makes the task considerably easier.
Alternatively, they can be safespotted on the wall east of the Ruins of Unkah.
summary: A Vannaka-only task at 50 combat. Crocodiles live along the River Elid south of Pollnivneach and around the Ruins of Unkah and Ruins of Ullek; they are aggressive melee slashers with poor drops, so most players just bring waterskins for the desert heat and either melee them or safespot them from across the water. Some crocodiles are confined to the water and can be safespotted by standing one tile back from the shore. The grassy area near the Ruins of Ullek has 12 spawns and needs no waterskins.
usefulItems: Ranged weapon (to hit crocodiles in the water)

locations.name: Stalker Den (multicombat)
locations.notes: Southern entrance (59 Agility) via quetzal to Auburnvale, Pendant of Ates to Nemus Retreat, or fairy ring AIS; northern entrance via fairy ring BLS or Xeric's Honour. Stalkers are already aggressive; step out every 10 minutes to reset aggression if not cannoning.

locations.name: Stalker Den (single-combat)
locations.notes: Elder stalkers are in the north (64 Agility stepping stone across the spring); juveniles can be safespotted behind a skeleton in the middle of their room and matures in the south-western single area once aggression drops.

strategy: Custodian stalkers are Slayer monsters found inside the Stalker Den that can be fought after the completion of the Shadows of Custodia quest. They can be assigned by Chaeldar, Mortimer, and Nieve. There are multicombat areas where cannons can be placed in the south-western side of the dungeon, and single-combat caverns in the south-eastern and northern parts.

The slayer stalkers all drop broken antlers, which are used to create Atlatl dart tips for creating atlatl darts outside of subduing the Moons of Peril. The mature and elder variants are also able to drop the antler guard, a powerful off-hand weapon boasting offensive stats in all styles, with no defence requirement to wield.
summary: Custodian stalkers are found only in the Stalker Den beneath the Custodia Pass after Shadows of Custodia; juveniles need 54 Slayer, matures 67 and elders 76. strategy: Dagannoth are a slayer task assigned by the advanced Slayer masters. Requiring completion of Horror from the Deep to be assigned, dagannoth are known for their high slayer experience rates and easy task completions. For players who are seeking a more difficult challenge, the Dagannoth Kings are a viable alternative for players of moderate to experienced combat ability.

The weaker variant of dagannoth can be found within the Lighthouse basement, Jormungand's Prison, and the Catacombs of Kourend. In the first two locations, a dwarf cannon can be used very effectively as the area is multicombat. For players who wish to maximise AFK time without relying on prayer, the lighthouse is a good choice. Otherwise, it is best to kill them in the prison or catacombs, as these two locations only house melee-using dagannoth. When killing the dagannoth in the Lighthouse, players can sell noted food to Jossik in the Lighthouse and buy it back in unnoted form for a small amount of money.

Players with prayer-boosting melee gear and a decent amount of prayer potions are able to AFK dagannoth within the Catacombs of Kourend with Auto Retaliate turned on. The only actions that require attention are restoring prayer points and walking away and back into the area should dagannoth become tolerant towards the player. While players cannot use a dwarf cannon in the Catacombs of Kourend, players can also use a Dinh's Bulwark special attack in conjunction with the 50% special attack regeneration from an equipped Lightbearer ring. Using the special attack from Dinh's Bulwark will help maintain enemy aggression without needing to leave the area to reset the aggression timer.
summary: Dagannoth are a fast, easy task once Horror from the Deep is done; they are much weaker than their combat level suggests. The Lighthouse basement and Jormungand's Prison are multicombat and are the standard cannon spots, with the Lighthouse offering some of the fastest Slayer XP in the game and the prison housing 62 melee-only dagannoth so Protect from Melee covers everything. The Catacombs of Kourend are multicombat but not cannonable and suit AFK melee with prayer. Waterbirth Island dagannoth are far stronger, and the Dagannoth Kings can be killed on the task.

They are all level 303, and also represent the combat triangle. Each of the kings uses a different combat style, is weak against the type that defeats them on the combat triangle, and has a high defence against all others. They all have their own, unique ring drops, with Rex having two - these rings give the second best bonuses for their respective combat styles in the ring slot. All three kings have the ability to drop the dragon axe, and also drop dagannoth bones.

- Dagannoth Rex - Attacks with Melee and is weak to Magic. Unique loot includes: berserker ring and warrior ring.
- Dagannoth Prime - Attacks with Magic and is weak to Ranged. Unique loot includes: seers ring and mud battlestaff.
- Dagannoth Supreme - Attacks with Ranged and is weak to Melee. Unique loot includes: archers ring and Seercull.
Killing all three Dagannoth Kings is a requirement for the Elite Fremennik Diary.

strategy: Dark beasts can be killed with Melee, Magic or Ranged. Melee is the most effective against them and should be used in conjunction with high prayer bonus armour, such as Proselyte armour, for Protect from Melee. To maximize profit, players should bring a herb sack and a gem bag so that they can loot all herbs and gems they receive.
Dark beasts are good point-gaining tasks as they are not assigned in large numbers; even the extension doesn't give as much as other monsters, though this is balanced by their large health pool.

Dark beasts are a unique monster in that they are permanently aggressive towards the player no matter how long they stay there for. They will only use Magic as their first attack if they are attacked by the player first, or if they cannot attack the player with Melee. As such, while they can be hit with a dwarf multicannon, it is not recommended to bring one. Not much attention is required for killing them, apart from restoring prayer, though players who have unlocked Superior slayer monsters will need to pay attention for any night beasts that spawn. Unlike their normal brethren, they are not aggressive and will always initiate with a magic attack even if forced to be made aggressive.
summary: Dark beasts need 90 Slayer and 90 combat and are permanently aggressive, never becoming tolerant. Melee with Protect from Melee and high prayer-bonus armour such as Proselyte is the standard method; they only open with Magic if you attack first or they cannot reach you, so a cannon is legal but not recommended. Both spots are single-way; the Mourner Tunnels hold 19 beasts and are reached instantly by Slayer ring after Mourning's End Part II, while the Iorwerth Dungeon has 10 and needs Song of the Elves but can drop crystal shards. Bring a herb sack and gem bag for the loot.

Some dark warriors can also be found in Great Kourend, accompanying necromancers. The warriors in Great Kourend are different combat levels than those found in the Wilderness.

Dark warriors found in the fortress come in both level 8 and 145 variants, the latter of which only appears in members' worlds. The area is multi-combat and a Dwarf multicannon can be set up in the centre of the inner courtyard of the fortress. To speed up a Krystilia Slayer task, it is recommended that the player kills the Level 8 Dark warriors roaming the corridors of the fortress, while leaving the cannon to deal with the Level 145 ones inside the courtyard, making sure to close the courtyard doors so that the warriors don't get out of range of the cannon by going inside the corridors.

Protect from Melee stops the swarm from overwhelming low-level players.

strategy: Drakes are high level Slayer monsters found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. They can drop their claws and teeth, which are used to upgrade the boots of stone and holy sandals into boots of brimstone and devout boots, respectively. These items are five times more common when killed on a Slayer task.

Drakes use both ranged and ranged melee, so melee armour is recommended against their attacks. Additionally, they will launch a fireball at the player's position, which deals 6-8 damage per hit for four hits if dragonfire protection is not used. It functions the same as chromatic dragonfire, although it can also be avoided by stepping away from the target tile.
Prior to completion of the elite Kourend & Kebos diary, boots of stone, boots of brimstone or granite boots must be worn within the dungeon to avoid taking constant damage.
summary: Drakes are level 84 Slayer wingless dragons on the middle level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, with a separate task-only room that the wiki recommends because it is smaller for a cannon. They use Ranged and ranged-melee attacks blocked by Protect from Missiles, plus a volcanic breath every seven attacks that dragonfire protection reduces or a one-tile sidestep avoids. Boots of stone, brimstone or granite boots are required in the dungeon unless the elite Kourend and Kebos diary is done. Melee with a dragon hunter lance is typical; many players block the task because of its high weight, lacklustre drops and the drakes' flat armour.

Dust devils are an incredibly popular task amongst most slayers, as they have a superior, the choke devil, and are often found in multicombat areas which allows for chinning and burst/barraging. They have relatively decent drops which usually covers the cost of supplies.

Unlike most monsters, dust devils attack with ranged melee; their attacks are considered melee, but they roll on the player's ranged defence rather than melee. They have low defence but are surprisingly accurate for their level.
summary: A very popular 65 Slayer task. A facemask or Slayer helmet must be worn or dust devils always hit 16 and drain your stats; with it they attack with ranged-based melee, so Protect from Melee or high ranged defence protects you. Most players burst or barrage (or chin) them in the multicombat south-east section of the Catacombs of Kourend, which is the easiest place to reach and has the catacombs drop table; the Smoke Dungeon has a quieter multi task-only area, and the Wilderness Slayer Cave is multi and cannonable but sits in level 25-28 Wilderness.

strategy: Earth warriors are a type of humanoid earth elemental found in a dirt-lined chamber in the Edgeville Dungeon. This area is in the Wilderness so it is advised to come prepared for player killers.
summary: A Krystilia-only Wilderness task. Level 51 earth warriors live in a dirt-lined chamber of the Edgeville Dungeon reached over monkey bars that need 15 Agility; the chamber spans level 7-10 Wilderness. They hit up to 5 with crush attacks and are slightly weaker to crush weapons and magic, and can be safespotted in the bottom-right corner or top of the first chamber. Bring food and an emergency teleport, and enable PK skull prevention in the settings so you cannot be skulled by mistake.

locations.name: Iorwerth Dungeon
locations.notes: 13 Iorwerth Warriors that drop crystal shards and enhanced crystal teleport seeds; monsters here do not need a task to be killed. Use the spaces around the fabric panels in the west of the room to trap the warriors north or south of you; they reach two tiles.

locations.name: Prifddinas
locations.notes: Pairs of halberd-wielding guards at the north, east, south and west gates (the east and north gates are close to a bank), 4 at the Tower of Voices entrances, 8 on the walkways above it and 3 in the market place. Gate guards can be safespotted by attacking from outside their wander radius and pushing them against the gate; market guards by shooting over Glenda or the spice stall bush. They drop crystal shards and enhanced crystal teleport seeds.

locations.name: Iorwerth Camp

locations.name: Lletya

Use the bench near the entrance or the poles in the village to trap the warriors. No notable drops besides crystal teleport seeds, but there is a bank and an altar.

strategy: Elves can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 70 combat by various Slayer masters after completion of Regicide. Elves either use ranged or melee, depending on their weapon; wielding either a crystal bow or a crystal halberd, of which the latter has an attack range of 2 tiles.

Until the player has access to Lletya, the only place for them to kill elves is the Iorwerth Camp. Reaching the camp can be very tedious without using an Iorwerth camp teleport, and players intending to use a dwarf multicannon are discouraged from doing so as the camp is impeded by tents, barrels, and crates. Players may prefer reanimating elves using the Arceuus spellbook spell Adept Reanimation at the Dark Altar, the ensouled heads being purchasable through the Grand Exchange, and gaining 754 Prayer experience per kill but gaining less Slayer and combat experience.

Once enough progress is made in Mourning's End Part I, players can kill elves in both Lletya and Mourner Headquarters. As with the Iorwerth Camp, getting to Lletya can be tedious, and the elves of Lletya have no notable drops other than Crystal teleport seeds. As for the Mourner Headquarters, only the level 108 mourners downstairs will count toward the task, and cannot be reached without a full set of mourner gear; the mourners upstairs do not count toward the task, despite all of them being elves.
summary: Assigned at 70 combat after Regicide by Vannaka, Chaeldar, Nieve and Duradel. Elves fight with a crystal bow or a crystal halberd that reaches two tiles, so keep at least two tiles between you and a warrior when safespotting. After Song of the Elves the Iorwerth Dungeon is the best spot: 13 Iorwerth Warriors that can be cannoned and trapped around the fabric panels in the west of the room, and they drop crystal shards and enhanced crystal teleport seeds. Before that only the Iorwerth Camp (and Lletya once Mourning's End Part I is started) is available; the task page recommends skipping elf tasks when possible because of their lower weight and the rarity of the seed drop.

trainingSummary.cons: Poor experience rates. Not worth doing unless Slayer points are an issue.
trainingSummary.pros: Relatively low-effort task.

locations.name: East of Chaos Temple (Wilderness)
locations.notes: 4 spawns (Ent LocLine pins). Reach with a burning amulet teleport to the Chaos Temple's north entrance in level 15 Wilderness and walk east. Elder chaos druids in the temple itself can teleblock players who get too close. In the Wilderness the trunk gives two noted logs per success.

locations.name: North of Chaos Temple (Wilderness)
locations.notes: 6 spawns (Ent LocLine pins), deeper than the eastern forest; same trunk-chopping mechanics. Do not bring anything you cannot afford to lose.

strategy: Ents are monsters found in the dungeon beneath the Woodcutting Guild and in the forests north and east of the Chaos Temple. Ents are found on members' worlds exclusively.

Upon death, the ent's trunk will fall and remain on the ground for 1 minute. These remains can be chopped to give several sets of noted logs according to the player's Woodcutting level. Players also have a chance to receive a bird nest while chopping the ent trunk. While cutting the trunk, players get 25 experience per set of logs received no matter the type. Completing the medium Wilderness Diary increases the chance of successfully chopping ents in the Wilderness by 15%. Ents can be safespotted by moving 1-3 tiles adjacent to a tree and using a ranged weapon, halberd, or magic attack.

Chopping the trunks requires an axe that the player has the Woodcutting level to use. The type of logs that can be received is determined by a player's base Woodcutting level, with higher levels giving better logs. The chance to successfully receive logs is determined by the player's current Woodcutting level (boosted or drained), with higher levels increasing success chance. The distribution of log types is determined by the axe used, with better axes providing a greater amount of higher tier logs.
summary: A Krystilia-only Wilderness task. Level 101 ents stand in the forests north and east of the Chaos Temple in the eastern Wilderness (Krystilia lists them at level 9-14 and 20-24). They are aggressive crush attackers that hit up to 10 with an attack range of 1 and have a 40% weakness to fire spells. Bring an axe: a dead ent's trunk can be chopped for noted logs for a minute (two logs per success in the Wilderness), and the medium Wilderness diary raises the chop success chance by 15%.
usefulItems: Axe (any you can use) to chop the trunk for noted logs

locations.name: Braindeath Island
locations.notes: The only place fever spiders exist. Talk to Pirate Pete at the dock north-east of Port Phasmatys (Ectophial then run north); the spiders are two tiles wide so many crate-edge safespots exist.

requiredItems: Slayer gloves (when being hit by the spiders)
strategy: Fever spiders are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 42 to kill, found only on Braindeath Island, in the brewery basement. This indirectly means players must also have started the Rum Deal quest in order to access them. Players must wear slayer gloves while fighting them, or face being damaged for 12.5% of their Hitpoints level and becoming diseased. Fever spiders are considered to be a relatively fast task due to the large quantity of spiders and their low Defence.

Players only need to wear slayer gloves if they are being hit by fever spiders, so players using Ranged or Magic may make use of safespots in order to wear better offensive gloves such as Barrows gloves. A notable safespot is located in the south-west corner, where players can trap the spiders on the edges of crates; however, due to the two tile wide nature of the spiders, many suitable safespots exist. Players safespotting the spiders without wearing slayer gloves are advised to bring a Relicym's balm in case the player accidentally becomes diseased.
summary: A 42 Slayer task from Vannaka and Chaeldar, done in the brewery basement of Braindeath Island, which needs Rum Deal started and is reached via Pirate Pete north of Port Phasmatys. Slayer gloves must be worn when the spiders hit you or you take 12.5% of your Hitpoints and become diseased; rangers and magers can safespot on the crate edges in the south-west corner and wear better gloves, carrying Relicym's balm in case of disease. The spiders have low Defence and there are many of them, so the task is quick.
usefulItems: Relicym's balm (if safespotting without slayer gloves)
Ectophial to reach Pirate Pete quickly

strategy: Fire giants can be assigned as a slayer task at level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They are the strongest generic giants for their category and are mostly known for their rune scimitar drops.

Fire giants can be found in an array of locations, most of which allow for the use of a dwarf multicannon. The lone exception is the Catacombs of Kourend, which does not allow a cannon but is a multicombat area.

In most cases, players are recommended to kill fire giants at the Catacombs of Kourend, due to the multicombat area of the dungeon allowing for relative AFK and having access to the catacombs drop table. The Giants' Den is a second alternative, as while it is not multicombat, it allows for a cannon and the giants are the same as those in the catacombs, along with sharing its drop-table including i.e. dark totem pieces. The level 109 Fire giants should be prioritised for maximum xp as they have more HP, yet significantly lower Defence levels compared to the level 104's.

locations.name: Stronghold of Security: Catacomb of Famine
locations.notes: 26 spawns of level 28, 35 and 41 crawlers in the rooms of the second level (Catacomb of Famine), reached through the Stronghold entrance in the Barbarian Village mine. Ranged safespots exist, such as the south-west corner of the south-east room, or hide behind non-aggressive giant rats. Count Check in the Lumbridge graveyard can teleport you to the entrance once.

strategy: Flesh Crawlers are medium level monsters found in the second level of the Stronghold of Security. They drop the bottom of sceptre, one of four parts of the skull sceptre. Flesh crawlers drop herbs often, and are frequently killed for their uncommon grimy ranarr drops.
They are scavengers, and will eat anything if given the chance.

Flesh crawlers are aggressive to any level players. Ranged is a good style to use as there are safespots in the rooms, such as in the south-west corner of the south-east room. It is possible to hide behind non-aggressive giant rats in one room and range the flesh crawlers, protected from their rapid, albeit weak, attacks. Their attack speed is three ticks, or equivalent to the goblin paint cannon. Because these attacks max at 1 damage, using a regen bracelet can help to offset much of the damage taken, especially if the player has a strong defence.

For minimal user-input (also known as afk or semi-afk training), turn on auto retaliate and let the crawlers come to you. When they lose their aggressiveness, simply move to another room, then come back. Since flesh crawlers are 2x2 in size, when multiple players are afk training at once the flesh crawlers can get stuck on one another and stop attacking the player; this can be mitigated by standing on the same tile as other players who are already afk training on the same world, greatly increasing xp rates.

To reduce banking trips needed, deposit all non-stackable drops when you are teleported to random events, and drop all herbs aside from ranarr, as those are often more valuable than even the highest levelled herbs such as dwarf weed.
summary: A low-level Mazchna task done on the second level of the Stronghold of Security (the Catacomb of Famine). Flesh crawlers are aggressive to everyone but max hit 1 with a fast three-tick attack, so turn on auto-retaliate and let them come to you, moving rooms when they stop being aggressive; a regen bracelet offsets the chip damage. They are 2x2 so they can get stuck on each other. They drop herbs often, including grimy ranarr, which makes them a popular low-level money maker.

requiredItems: Elemental shield, mind shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward or ancient wyvern shield
strategy: Fossil Island Wyverns are a Slayer monster requiring 66 Slayer to kill. A combat level of 60, as well as the completion of the quests Elemental Workshop and Bone Voyage, is required for them to be assigned as a slayer task.

Similarly to their skeletal cousins, Fossil Island Wyverns use both melee and an icy breath. The icy breath requires the use of an elemental shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield in order to take reduced damage from the breath; the latter also provides immunity from being frozen. Protect from Magic can also be used but only provides half the damage reduction of the prior protections. Antifire potions of any type and the anti-dragon shield do not work to mitigate icy breath.
There are four types of wyverns that fall under this category, of which three can be fought at 66 Slayer and the other at 82 Slayer.
summary: A 66 Slayer task in the Wyvern Cave on Fossil Island, requiring Bone Voyage and Elemental Workshop to be assigned. The wyverns use melee and an icy breath that must be reduced with an elemental, mind, dragonfire or ancient wyvern shield (antifire and the anti-dragon shield do nothing); only the ancient wyvern shield stops the freeze. Tank them with high ranged defence and Protect from Melee, prioritising Spitting Wyverns and Long-tailed Wyverns (fight the latter in melee range) and avoiding Taloned and Ancient Wyverns, which use a typeless ranged attack from any distance. The task is unprofitable and many players buy the Stop the Wyvern unlock to block it.
