locations.name: Grimstone Dungeon
locations.notes: The only location for frost dragons. The dragons are in the centre of the dungeon, reached by climbing up the rock face from the north or south (the south climb needs 83 Agility, boostable). Loot spawns on the dragon's central north-eastern tile. Off-task attacks on the western cave give the message 'You feel a strange coldness wash over you'.
requirements: 87 Sailing to reach Grimstone (fairy ring DLP after mooring once)

requiredItems: Anti-dragon shield with antifire potion, or super antifire potion (dragonfire shield/ward or ancient wyvern shield also listed)
strategy: Frost dragons are a type of adult dragon located in the dungeon on the island of Grimstone, requiring 87 Sailing to access. A combat level of 85 is required to be assigned them as a slayer task, along with the Sailing requirement to access the island. Once players have moored on the island at least once, it can also be accessed via fairy ring code fairy ring DLP.

Like chromatic dragons, frost dragons attack with melee and short-ranged dragonfire. However, they differ in several respects: their melee defences are weakest to crush, then stab, rather than stab alone; they have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells rather than 50% to water spells; and while heavy ranged remains the best ranged option, they are more resistant to ranged attacks overall. As with all dragons, they are weak to dragonbane weapons.

Additionally, their dragonfire is considered icy, and will briefly freeze the player if they do not have adequate protection. This icy dragonfire can be partially negated by a regular antifire potion, or fully negated using either a regular antifire potion with an anti-dragon shield, or with a super antifire potion alone. Because they only use melee and short-ranged dragonfire, frost dragons can be safespotted.
summary: Assigned by Nieve and Duradel at 85 combat, but you need 87 Sailing to reach Grimstone; after mooring there once, fairy ring DLP takes you straight into the Grimstone Dungeon. Frost dragons use melee and a short-range icy dragonfire that freezes you unless fully protected by an antifire potion with an anti-dragon shield or a super antifire alone, and because both attacks are short range they can be safespotted. They are 100% weak to fire spells, weakest to crush then stab, and take extra damage from dragonbane weapons; a task-only cave to the west of the main area has extra spawns.

trainingSummary.cons: Mediocre experience rates. Requires travelling with a boat that can withstand icy seas when visiting for the first time.
trainingSummary.pros: Relatively low-effort task. Decent profit.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Do for profit; skip for XP

strategy: Ghosts can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 13 combat by Turael, Spria, and Mazchna. Ghosts spawn in various locations throughout Gielinor.
Only regular ghosts, forgotten souls, tortured souls, death wings and Revenants can be killed to satisfy the task. Spectres, ghasts, banshees and shades will not count towards the task.

Most areas that contain ghosts contain those of combat levels 19, 24, and 29. Ghosts with a combat level of 76 and 77 can only be found in the Sepulchre of Death, the bottom floor of the Stronghold of Security.
summary: A beginner task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna at 13 combat. Ghosts are undead, so Crumble Undead and the salve amulet work well, and they drop nothing in most places. Level 19-29 ghosts are scattered across many areas; the Catacombs of Kourend has 17 in a multicombat area and the Sepulchre of Death at the bottom of the Stronghold of Security has 31 level 76-77 ghosts for the most XP per kill. Tortured souls near the Ectofuntus are the task page's pick for mid-levels with Morytania access. Spectres, ghasts, banshees and shades do not count.

locations.name: South of the Slayer Tower
locations.notes: 12 ghoul spawns (12 LocLine pins) on the grounds south of the Slayer Tower and west of Canifis; the Canifis page says 'The northern ghoul grounds features 12 ghouls, great for Slayer tasks'. Reach it via the Kharyrll Teleport (Canifis bank), a Slayer ring to the Slayer Tower entrance north of the town, or fairy ring CKS just west of Canifis (Canifis page teleport list).

locations.name: North of Mort Myre Swamp
locations.notes: 10 ghouls (10 LocLine pins) walk the Salve graveyard 'just north of the swamp' (Canifis). The Salve Graveyard Teleport lands 'slightly west of the town' and fairy ring CKS is nearby. The Ghoul page's safespot 'between two gravestones and a cross on the eastern side, directly north from the Large grave' is described for 'the ghouls to the west of Canifis' without naming the cluster; the Large grave page places one large grave at the eastern edge of this cluster (3434,3457) and another south of the Slayer Tower cluster (3413,3495), so it may apply to either. Retreating ghouls 'walk back to the water and will still be within range'.

strategy: Ghouls are found just west of Canifis, north of the swamp and west of the fairy ring code fairy ring CKS. Though they may appear to be undead and are often mistaken for such, they are in fact still alive and thus immune to both the Crumble Undead spell and to the effects of the salve amulet and salve amulet (e). A ghoul bone is needed to complete the Rag and Bone Man II. Killing a ghoul is a requirement for the easy Morytania Diary.

Ghouls can be somewhat troublesome to kill. When a ghoul has low hitpoints, it will stop attacking the player and retreat, allowing other ghouls to attack. Applying poison can be an effective method of killing the previous ghoul whilst attacking the next one.

It is possible for a ghoul to randomly attack a player lower than level 85 combat, ignoring any current engagement that player may be in. This is especially annoying as you won't be able to secure the kill to get the Slayer experience, because the game will say

An efficient way to kill a ghoul can be through magic or ranged. Melee is possible, but remember, they do flee when their health gets low. The effect of their retreat can be minimised by spending 10 minutes in the area (either while using magic or ranged, or simply waiting) for the Ghouls to become tolerant so that other Ghouls will not attack.

The ghouls to the west of Canifis are safespottable using the gravestones. A very useful safespot is between two gravestones and a cross on the eastern side, directly north from the Large grave. Any ghoul from the north-east gets stuck on the northern gravestone. Keeping you from being attacked while shooting ghouls over the gravestones. When retreating, they will walk back to the water and will still be within range.

If a player lures one of the two south-most ghouls to the south-west of the ghoul area, just to the left of the west-most plant, the player can run to the north side of the ghoul, effectively trapping it in that corner. The ghoul will be unable to retreat as the player will move with it as it tries to run away, and continue to block it from moving further. Occasionally, another ghoul will get close enough to interrupt the final blows of the fight, but the player can run south of the almost dead ghoul and keep it trapped between the player and the aggressive ghoul.
summary: A low-level Mazchna and Vannaka task fought just west of Canifis in Morytania. Ghouls hit up to 5 with crush, are aggressive, and run away when their hitpoints get low, so ranged or magic from behind the gravestones (or poison) is the easiest way to secure kills; melee works but expect them to flee. They look undead but are alive, so the salve amulet and Crumble Undead do nothing. Both the Salve graveyard north of Mort Myre and the grounds south of the Slayer Tower have about a dozen spawns each, and a ghoul may randomly attack players under combat level 85.

strategy: Greater demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve/Steve, and Duradel/Kuradal. Despite their "greater" status, they possess a somewhat lackluster drop table, with their two most valuable drops being the rune full helm and the hard clue scroll. There are many different types of greater demons residing around Gielinor; however, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave, all have the same drop table.

When not killing greater demons as part of Konar or Krystilia's tasks, players have many spots to choose from. The most common spots are the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The Chasm of Fire is a cannonable area in a small space, allowing for plenty of AFK and fast kill times, along with contracts for challenging a stronger version of Yama. Catering to the increased drop rates will require more banking and less AFK time, however. The Catacombs of Kourend has access to the ancient shard and dark totem piece drops. It is also a Multicombat area, allowing for players to AFK until the aggression timer expires, which can be easily reset.

In the Wilderness, players have several spots to kill greater demons from. The most common would be the Wilderness Slayer Cave due to the enhanced drops, multiway area and allowing a cannon, but this spot is frequented often by player killers, so players should not bring items they are not willing to lose. The Demonic Ruins is a much worse spot, due to being a far deeper multiway area and players tend to teleport in via Annakarl Teleports. A more secluded spot is the Lava Maze Dungeon, but accessing it requires a long trek around the maze, or 82 Agility (boostable at 77) for a shortcut that cuts a significant amount of time.

The Chasm of Fire is the usual spot because it is compact and cannonable (single-way), while the Catacombs of Kourend are multicombat for AFK burst/venator killing plus ancient shard and dark totem drops. Wilderness tasks are best done in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, which is both multi and cannonable but heavily PKed.

They attack with melee and dragonfire, thus some protection against it should be considered. Due to their large size, they are usually able to be safespotted with ranged or halberd-like weapons. strategy: Gryphons can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer after completion of the Troubled Tortugans quest. Additionally, both Nieve and Duradel may assign gryphons after the perk Wings Spread has been purchased.

Gryphons are found exclusively on The Great Conch. There are three lairs for gryphons; a western cavern, an eastern cavern (Slayer task only) and a lair in the centre of the island which leads to the Shellbane gryphon. Both the eastern and western caverns have a southern room that is multi-combat and cannon-able.

Gryphons attack with melee and have a special attack which causes knockback and moderate damage if the player's weight of their worn equipment is too low; this is 30 for normal gryphons and 40 for the boss. They are weakest to melee, ideally from stabbing attacks. While being a bit more resistant to magic, they have a 50% weakness to air spells.
summary: A 51 Slayer task on the Great Conch (Troubled Tortugans and 45 Sailing) from Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer, or Nieve/Duradel after buying Wings Spread. Gryphons melee and have a knockback special that hurts if your equipped weight is under 30 kg, so wear heavy gear; they are weakest to stab melee and 50% weak to air spells. The best method is the south-western multicombat room of the eastern task-only cave with a cannon and a venator bow or melee; the western cave has a full safespot. A tortugan shield is only required for the dire gryphon superior and the Shellbane gryphon boss.

strategy: Harpie bug swarms are mid-level slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 33 to kill. A lit bug lantern, which requires a Firemaking level of 33 to light, is required to damage these monsters (the lantern must be lit and equipped). If you do not have 33 Firemaking, you cannot be assigned harpie bug swarms as a Slayer task.

Harpie bug swarms should be an easy task for well-equipped mid-level players; their abundance as well as the fact that they remain aggressive to players until level 93 combat makes this task very click-easy. As harpie bug swarms are very accurate, and will often hit for up to 6 Hitpoints, it is advisable to have Defence levels from 40-50+ and to bring food appropriate for the player's level, such as lobsters. Another option is to keep Protect from Melee up and recharge prayer at the relatively nearby altars.
It is recommended to bring nature runes while slaying this monster since it has many drops that can be alched to free up inventory spaces, and fire runes are frequently dropped from this monster.

strategy: Hellhounds can be assigned as a slayer task at 65 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular hellhounds only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times. Hellhounds are primarily known for their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls, at a rate of 1/64, or 1/32 if killing in the Wilderness with a imbued ring of wealth. They also drop ensouled hellhound heads and the smouldering stone.

Outside of the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Stronghold Slayer Cave for general slayer, as there are four rooms of three or four hellhounds in each one, and a dwarf multicannon can be set up in their caves. They may also be killed in the Catacombs of Kourend for ancient shards and dark totem pieces. The catacombs do not allow for a cannon, but is a Multicombat area and allows for relative AFK training, especially with a Venator bow, and is also quite close to the entrance. Once the aggression timer expires, the player can simply run south and up the vine to the Giants' Den to reset aggression. Some players opt to restore prayer at an altar and teleport back to this location using Xeric's talisman's Xeric's Heart option or the Kourend Castle Teleport spell (requires 48 Magic and completion of Client of Kourend to unlock the spell).

In the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, with a group of five slightly stronger hellhounds in a multicombat area. The drop rate of the smouldering stone from these hellhounds is increased by 50%, and they have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table, which can help offset some supply costs. However, the cave itself is a very popular player killing hotspot despite the hellhounds being below level 20 Wilderness, and players killing them here should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose. These hellhounds are generally killed if assigned by Krystilia.
summary: A mid-to-high level task from Vannaka, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, Duradel and Krystilia. Hellhounds only bite with accurate melee, so either safespot them (they are 2x2 and get stuck on rocks) or keep Protect from Melee on; they are demons, so Arclight/Emberlight work well. The Stronghold Slayer Cave is the standard spot (four rooms, task-only, cannon allowed), the Catacombs of Kourend are multicombat for AFK venator bow or burst plus ancient shard and totem drops, and Wilderness tasks are done in the Wilderness Slayer Cave. Their draw is the 1/64 hard clue rate (1/32 with an imbued ring of wealth in the Wilderness).

trainingSummary.cons: Commonly assigned and long task. Using the cannon will result in a loss due to lack of drops. Killing Cerberus effectively requires expensive equipment, and the profit is very inconsistent due to the value mostly being in the rare unique drops.
trainingSummary.pros: Cerberus can be killed on task for good long-term profit. Relatively low-effort task if killing regular hellhounds, and good source of hard clue scrolls.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Block unless killing Cerberus for profit

strategy: Hydras can be assigned as a slayer task at level 95 Slayer. This is a task exclusive to both Konar and Mortimer; the latter requires partial completion of Fallen From Grace.

Mortimer is the best way for players to obtain hydra tasks. Not only does Mortimer assign more on average, he also has various incentives when completing these tasks from him, such as additional kills, increased clue scrolls or superior drop rates. Given the nature of his assignments however, players should try to complete the task accordingly to benefit from the incentive. Mortimer has a small pool of tasks, and coupled with his unique ability for the player to assign themselves appropriately from two or three (after completing 50 tasks with him), means it is very easy to be given hydras from him. Assuming that every task can be offered with two of the normal tasks (which have a weight of 10) are blocked, there is a 4.0% chance for hydras to be offered.

Konar, the original master who could assign hydras, has a huge pool despite having a total lower weight of 250. To get the best possible chance to be given a hydra task, the player must block a lot of other tasks, especially ones that are the same, close to or higher than hers, such as metal dragons, drakes and wyrms (both of which share the same weight as hydra tasks). Because of the larger pool of tasks and traditional slayer assignments, it is harder to get a task from Konar compared to Mortimer, and the only incentive for completing the task from Konar are slayer points and the chance for brimstone keys.
summary: A 95 Slayer task from Konar and Mortimer, found only on the lower level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Hydras alternate ranged and magic in sets of one to three attacks and later spit poison pools, so start with the protection prayer for your weaker defence and swap when they switch; ranged (twisted bow) or a dragonbane weapon is standard because of their very high magic level. Wear boots of stone, brimstone or granite unless you have the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary. The Alchemical Hydra boss can be killed instead while on task and is far more profitable.

strategy: Ice giants can be assigned as a Slayer task at 50 combat by Vannaka and Krystilia. They are the second strongest generic giants for their category, only slightly stronger than their mossy counterparts, with very slight defensive bonuses and having a 100% weakness to fire spells.
Ice giant tasks are generally not completed by players not training via Wilderness Slayer, as they have very unimpressive drops and many of them are far from a bank.

They are primarily killed as part of Krystilia's Slayer tasks, as a cluster of 14 slightly stronger ice giants can be found in the Wilderness Slayer Cave. These giants are found below level 20 Wilderness and are cannonable in a multicombat area, making it a very quick task for plenty of points. As the cave is a popular player killing spot, players should not take items they are unwilling to lose. Normal ice giants can be found at the Frozen Waste Plateau, but escape is next to impossible if caught by a player killer.

strategy: Ice warriors are mid-level ice elementals. They have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells. Ice warriors can be assigned by Krystilia for a Wilderness Slayer task, or by Vannaka or Mazchna for normal tasks.
Kamil fought during Desert Treasure I is considered an ice warrior for a Slayer assignment.

Ice warriors have good accuracy and can cut through Ranged and Magic armour with ease. They also seem to have higher levels of aggression than many other mobs as they'll often engage the player from a rather long distance. If using melee, wearing at least adamant or rune armour and using high quality food is advised.

Fire spells are extremely strong against ice warriors. Using fire bolt with chaos gauntlets is an economical option and gives you a max hit of 30. If you receive ice warriors as a Slayer task, using your best fire spell will most likely be the fastest way to complete the task.

In the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, they can be safespotted by trapping an ice warrior on one side of a plus-shaped formation of rocks (not to be confused with the floor ice spikes) in the north-western area of their room.

At the White Wolf Mountain they can be safespotted south of the middle dungeon marker outside of the triple ladder enclosure, though there are level 25 and 38 wolves which will be aggressive unless the player's combat level exceeds double their level.
summary: Low-level ice elementals assigned by Mazchna, Vannaka and Krystilia. They are aggressive, accurate slashers that cut through ranged and magic armour, so melee in adamant or rune with decent food is advised; fire spells are extremely strong against them and the wiki says your best fire spell is most likely the fastest way through the task. The closest spot is the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon south of Port Sarim, where they can be safespotted behind a plus-shaped rock formation; the Frozen Waste Plateau is the Wilderness option.

strategy: Infernal Mages are Slayer monsters that require 45 Slayer to kill. They are mainly hunted for their unique drops: the fire ruby, and the rare dark mystic boots and hat drops, and are sometimes hunted for their frequent drops of death runes. Players who plan on fighting them should be wary of their accurate magic attack, although Protect from Magic negates this completely.

To reach the Infernal Mage area in the 1st floor of the Slayer Tower, players can take the long way up the south-east stairs, which requires running past aggressive Banshees, so wearing Earmuffs or a Slayer helmet is recommended. Players with 18 Agility Agility can avoid the banshees by using the broken window shortcut for quick access to the stairs.
summary: A 45 Slayer task assigned by Vannaka and Mortimer, done on the first floor of the Slayer Tower. Infernal mages are not aggressive and attack only with an accurate magic attack that Protect from Magic negates completely. Getting to them means running past aggressive banshees, so wear earmuffs or a Slayer helmet, or use the 18 Agility broken-window shortcut. They are mainly killed for fire rubies, death runes and rare dark mystic boots and hat.
usefulItems: Earmuffs or Slayer helmet (banshees on the way up)

strategy: TzTok-Jad (translated as Hard/Rock/Obsidian Fire Elemental), commonly called Jad for short, is a volcanic creature and the boss of the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame.

With a combat level of 702, TzTok-Jad has a max hit of 97 and can easily kill most players in one hit with any of its three attacks: a Melee attack with its bite (max hit of 97), a blast of Magic in the form of a fireball (max hit of 95), and a boulder falling from the ceiling as a Ranged attack (max hit of 97). To add to the challenge, players must fight through waves of monsters in the TzHaar Fight Cave in order to reach TzTok-Jad and must do so solo and without being able to restock on supplies from the previous waves.
TzTok-Jad is the boss monster of the TzHaar Fight Cave, and is encountered on Wave 63 (the final wave).

Once TzTok-Jad is reached, fighting and defeating him requires decent skill and reflexes. It is possible to engage TzTok-Jad using Melee, but as TzTok-Jad's melee attack has no warning animation, players must have Protect from Melee active when in melee distance, and switch to Protect from Missiles or Protect from Magic once the respective warning animation is identified. Note though that Jad can attack with melee every, as opposed to its normal attack speed. When at a distance, TzTok-Jad only uses Ranged and Magic attacks, which can hit the player from up to 15 tiles away. While Jad has no defence bonuses, it is recommended to kill Jad with ranged, as it avoids the melee attack completely, only leaving the magic and ranged attacks for Jad.

As with all other off-colored monsters in the Fight Caves, locating where the orange Ket-Zek spawned will indicate Jad's spawn point. Like the Tok-Xil, Jad has a very long attack range, and players not using drawn out clients can find themselves being attacked by Jad without seeing the combat style he uses and where he comes from.

Like Ket-Zek, Jad's attacks can deal extremely high damage, and is even capable of killing lower-leveled players in one hit if not protected against. Jad's melee and ranged attacks have a max hit of 97, while the magic attack has a max hit of 95.

- Melee: TzTok-Jad thrusts forward with a sharp bite. He only does this if the player is within melee distance. Unlike the Magic and Ranged attacks, the Melee attack is instant.
- Magic: TzTok-Jad rears up on his hind legs and dangles his forward legs for a few seconds before launching a fireball from his mouth at the player.
- Ranged: TzTok-Jad rears up on his…
summary: TzTok-Jad is the boss of the TzHaar Fight Cave under the Karamja Volcano in Mor Ul Rek; after unlocking Hot Stuff, Chaeldar, Nieve or Duradel may offer 1-3 Jad kills in place of a TzHaar task, and leaving or dying in the cave ends the task without breaking your streak.

They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.
It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.
Two stronger variants of jellies can be found on Zeah; the Warped Jelly in the Catacombs of Kourend, and the Chilled jelly in the Ruins of Tapoyauik/Grimstone Dungeon.

strategy: Jungle horrors are horrors that live on the island of Mos Le'Harmless. Players must have completed Cabin Fever to gain access to the island. They can be assigned as a Slayer task by Chaeldar and Vannaka. They are a weaker relative of the cave horrors that live inside the caves on the island. A witchwood icon is NOT required to kill jungle horrors.
Players with under level 70 Defence are advised to bring food (lobsters or better) and armour to negate the jungle horror's relatively accurate melee attacks.

Alternatively, players with a high Defence level can sustain themselves by cutting jungle horrors' commonly dropped pineapples. Simply bring a knife to cut it into pineapple slices. This will heal 8 Hitpoints per pineapple. The NPC Joe right next to the gate sells stews and wine.

There is a single spawn near the opening in the northern Mos Le'Harmless wall which will not run away when damaged from behind the wall and can thus be easily safespotted. There is a set of spawns on the north-east corner of the wall which will not run away when using ranged or magic and can be safespotted. There are also many plants and trees which can be used to safespot several different jungle horror spawns slightly west of Mos Le'Harmless' northern gate.
summary: Jungle horrors are aggressive melee (stab) attackers on the island of Mos Le'Harmless, assigned by Vannaka and Chaeldar; no witchwood icon is needed, unlike cave horrors. Players under 70 Defence should bring good food and armour against their accurate melee, while higher-level players can sustain off the pineapples they drop with a knife. The biggest camp of 10-12 is directly north of the settlement's exit and several spawns can be safespotted from behind the northern wall or trees.

strategy: Kalphites can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 combat by all Slayer masters, with the exception of Mortimer and the Wilderness Slayer master Krystilia. Kalphites come in a wide variety of levels, which is why they are possible tasks from all Slayer masters. They can be found in the Kalphite Lair in the north-west Kharidian Desert, as well as in a Slayer task-exclusive area, the Kalphite Cave, just east of Shantay Pass.

Kalphites comes in four varieties: workers, soldiers, and guardians, as well as the boss monster the Kalphite Queen. With the exception of the Queen, all Kalphites use melee attacks. Additionally the soldiers and guardians can induce poison starting at 4 and 6 Hitpoints damage respectively. This poison bypasses protection prayers. Protect from Melee and some type of poison immunity will completely negate damage from the workers, soldiers and guardians.
summary: A common task from every master except Mortimer and Krystilia. If Konar forces the Kalphite Lair, cannon the soldiers on the upper level; the Queen is not worth it without the Elite Desert Diary shortcut.

strategy: The Kalphite Queen (Kalphiscarabeinae pasha), also called the KQ, is the strongest of the Kalphites.

She is a powerful opponent that makes use of protection prayers, though they only function as an indicator to players of which attack styles may be most effective rather than outright blocking damage from them. She can use all three combat styles, of which her ranged and magic attacks always land as successful hits, and has two forms.

Unique drops from the Queen include the dragon 2h sword, dragon chainbody, dragon pickaxe and kq head drops. Killing her is additionally a requirement for the Desert Diary, with a hard task requiring players to kill her once and an elite task requiring the player to speak to a mounted head inside their own Player-owned house.

requiredItems: Insulated boots
strategy: Killerwatts are Slayer monsters located in the Killerwatt plane, accessible through a portal at the top floor of Draynor Manor after completion of Ernest the Chicken. A Slayer level of 37 is required to kill them.

If a player is not wearing a pair of insulated boots while fighting them, both their Ranged and Melee attacks will have a much higher maximum hit. Even when wearing insulated boots, their attacks are still rapid and highly accurate. A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Killerwatt plane.
Killerwatts are a commonly skipped Slayer task due to their relatively high damage output combined with their mediocre drops, except for those seeking their unique air diamond drop.

While Killerwatts initially appear as passive floating orbs of electricity, they will immediately transform and move towards you when clicked on, rather than when attacked. They will switch between attacking with melee and ranged, depending on the player's distance from them and whether or not they are able to attack the player. For example, attacking a Killerwatt in melee range and then safespotting it will result in it switching to ranged attacks.

It is recommended to use either Ranged or Magic against them due to their negative ranged defences and weakness to air spells, as well as being able to easily restrict the Killerwatts to ranged attacks. Melee can be used as well if using a weapon such as a Halberd, as careful use of their extra range lets you lock the Killerwatts into using ranged attacks.
The Killerwatt's damage bonus from the player not wearing insulated boots does not hit through the correct protection prayer.
summary: A 37 Slayer task assigned only by Mazchna, done on the Killerwatt plane reached through Professor Oddenstein's portal at the top of Draynor Manor after Ernest the Chicken. Insulated boots are required: without them both their melee and ranged attacks hit up to 15 instead of 6 and 8, though the bonus does not go through the correct protection prayer. They appear as passive orbs but transform and rush you as soon as they are clicked, and switch between melee and ranged by distance, so Ranged or Magic (air spells) from a safespot locks them into ranged attacks.

strategy: The Kraken is a stronger and larger version of the cave kraken. It requires level 87 Slayer to kill and cannot be boosted. Located at the Kraken Cove, it can only be attacked if the player has it, or cave krakens as a Slayer task, which also requires level 50 Magic. Alongside its non-boss variants, it is the only monster that drops the trident of the seas and Kraken tentacle.

Like its smaller brethren, the Kraken is submerged underwater. Magic is the only reliable way of damaging it, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage. The Kraken cannot be reached with Melee weapons, and is additionally entirely immune to melee attacks, displaying the message if you were to hit it with a melee weapon with long enough range to reach it. To start the fight, players can use a fishing explosive on the large whirlpool. Otherwise, the four whirlpools around must first be disturbed; when all four whirlpools are disturbed, the larger one can be disturbed, which will result in the Kraken waking up. Either method will release level 112 Enormous Tentacles.

Both the Kraken and Enormous Tentacles use typeless Magic, and as such Protect from Magic does not provide any degree of damage reduction. The Kraken can hit very hard, but has very poor accuracy, while the tentacles are much more accurate but deal less damage. The Kraken's projectile resembles Fire Wave.

He is located in Zamorak's Fortress, which requires 70 Hitpoints to cross the river to access. To gain access to his chamber, players must use an ecumenical key or have slain 40 Zamorakians throughout the dungeon.

strategy: Kurask are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 70 to kill. Like turoth, they can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad ammunition, or the Magic Dart spell due to their tough hides; they are immune to any other types of attacks. They are, however, susceptible to burn damage from weapons such as burning claws.

Kurask are relatively inaccurate, but they can hit somewhat high if their attacks manage to land. Additionally, they have fast health regeneration, healing one hitpoint every five game ticks. Due to their relative inaccuracy, they can be fought without protection prayers by using Bones to Peaches for healing, though players may wish to activate Protect from Melee if the superior version, the king kurask, spawns.

Although kurask are invulnerable to any damage from the special attacks of Saradomin godsword, ancient godsword, and toxic blowpipe, their healing effects will still activate as if damage had been dealt, making them useful as special attack weapons during extended trips. Likewise, the special attacks of ancient mace and eldritch Nightmare staff will restore prayer points based on what damage would have been dealt. The set effect of Guthan's equipment will not activate against kurask, however.
summary: Kurask require 70 Slayer and can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows or bolts, or Magic Dart; everything else (including cannons and thralls) deals no damage. They hit inaccurately with crush up to 11, so most players melee with a leaf-bladed battleaxe under Protect from Melee, or skip prayer and heal with Bones to Peaches. The Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (fairy ring AJR) has 5 kurask plus a 9-spawn task-only area; the Iorwerth Dungeon (Song of the Elves) has 14 tightly grouped kurask that also drop crystal shards. Bring an herb sack and alch runes since the task is profitable.

trainingSummary.cons: Can only be harmed with leaf-bladed weaponry, broad bolts or Magic Dart, which results in poor experience rates. Not worth doing for XP unless Slayer points are an issue.
trainingSummary.pros: Somewhat decent profit.

strategy: Lava dragons are former red dragons that have been transformed after being surrounded by lava for too long. They reside in the Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness (between level 36 and 42 Wilderness), and attack with melee as well as with dragonfire. Due to their low Magic level they are particularly weak to Magic, which combined with their weakness to water spells makes water bolt a slow but profitable method of killing them.

Lava dragons can be safespotted both inside and outside their isle. The many piles of skeletons and edges at the isle allow for players to safespot them inside. Alternatively, players can camp some of the southern spawns outside the isle. Having 74 Agility is recommended when killing them to use the stepping stones to escape the isle, as the area is frequented by player killers.

Bringing a pestle and mortar is optional to grind the scales into shards, in addition to High Level Alchemy runes to alch their common adamant and rune equipment drops. If killing them from outside the isle, Telekinetic Grab will be needed to grab their drops. Although it is possible to stay at the isle indefinitely using this method, it is advisable to bank every 10–20 minutes as the isle is commonly targeted by player killers.
summary: A Krystilia-only Wilderness task at Lava Dragon Isle (level 36-42 Wilderness), a multicombat area with 8 dragons. They melee up to 23 and breathe dragonfire up to 50, so bring an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield plus antifire, and use Magic (they have 1 Magic level and a 50% water weakness) or Ranged from the many skeleton-pile safespots inside the isle or from the southern spawns outside it. The isle is above level 30 Wilderness, so no teleports work; 74 Agility unlocks the southern stepping-stone shortcut.

strategy: Lesser demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, and Vannaka. They are combat level 82, 87, and 94 and all have the same drop table, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave.
When not killing lesser demons as part of a Krystilia task, players have many spots to choose from to kill lesser demons.

The most common spots would be the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The former can drop contracts after speaking to Yama after A Kingdom Divided, which makes killing the demons there much more lucrative compared to any other spot. However, catering to the preferred method will slow down times. There are four demons in a very small area, which allows for easy AFK times. The demons in the Catacombs are in a multicombat area and can be AFK'ed with access to the catacombs table, but a dwarf multicannon is not allowed. If none of these locations are available, it is best to kill them in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon; the southern area contains six lesser demons with a fair amount of safespots and allows a cannon.
summary: A low-value task from Krystilia, Vannaka or Chaeldar; lesser demons hit with slash only, have low Defence and are weak to demonbane weapons. Outside the Wilderness the Chasm of Fire (fairy ring DJR, 9 demons, cannonable, safespots, Yama contracts after A Kingdom Divided) and the Catacombs of Kourend (8 demons, multicombat, no cannon, ancient shards and totem pieces) are the usual picks. For a Krystilia task the Wilderness Slayer Cave is the only reasonable spot: 7 demons with a better drop table, cannonable and multicombat, below level 30 so a one-click teleport escapes.

Players have three options when assigned Lesser Nagua, depending on their quest completion:

- Players who have completed Perilous Moons can be assigned to kill Nagua at Neypotzli, where Sulphur Nagua can be found.
- Players who have completed The Heart of Darkness can be assigned to kill Nagua at the Ruins of Tapoyauik, where Frost Nagua and Amoxliatl can be found.
- Players who have completed The Final Dawn can also be assigned to kill Nagua at the Crypt of Tonali, where Earthen Nagua can be found.
summary: A 48 Slayer task from Chaeldar or Konar after Perilous Moons, popular as AFK melee. All lesser nagua have -4 flat armour so every hit deals 4 extra damage, making fast or multi-hit weapons like the dual macuahuitl ideal. Sulphur nagua at Neypotzli are the default: supplies are free there (moonlight potions restore prayer and boost melee, bream and moss lizard are food), a cannon can be placed and there are safespots, though they drain 5 prayer if you stand in melee range during their wind-up. Frost nagua (Ruins of Tapoyauik, The Heart of Darkness) are magic attackers negated by Protect from Magic, and earthen nagua (Tonali Cavern, The Final Dawn) become weak to crush below 60% health.

strategy: Lizardman can be assigned as a Slayer task after being unlocked at a cost of 75 Slayer reward points via the Reptile got ripped ability.

Normal lizardmen come in three forms; a plain level 53 and 62 variant, and the level 75 lizardman brute. These are simple enemies and have a weak poison that starts at 3 damage. They have very few lucrative drops, so these variants are primarily killed for the sake of speeding through a task with a cannon, often at the Lizardman Canyon due to it being a multicombat area.

The stronger shamans can be found in more sparse locations, and are more commonly killed as they drop the valuable dragon warhammer, which is popular for players who cannot acquire an elder maul. Lizardmen shamans require the use of Shayzien armour in order to kill them, as they have a unique poison spit that can deal up to 30 damage, which is fully blocked while wearing a full set of tier 5 shayzien armour. They also have various mechanics that make them harder to kill, though they are still easily dealt with using a ranged weapon and Protect from Missiles.
summary: Only assignable after buying 'Reptile got ripped' for 75 points from Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve or Duradel. Plain lizardmen and brutes are weak, poisonous (3) crush/ranged attackers with poor drops, so the task is usually blitzed with a cannon at the multicombat Lizardman Canyon east side (34 lizardmen plus 28 brutes). Players hunting the dragon warhammer kill lizardman shamans instead, ideally in the Lizardman Temple under Molch where the spawn explosions and jump AoE are smaller; shamans need Shayzien armour (tier 5 fully blocks the 25-30 acid spit) and Protect from Missiles at range. Killing lizardmen does not progress a normal Lizards task.

strategy: The Maggot King is a boss in Vampyrium that requires completion of The Blood Moon Rises to kill. The entrance to its lair can be found in the forest east of Sangvesti, near the Ruined Village.

Players may only fight the boss by themselves, and the fight takes place inside an instance. Additionally, a mix of melee and either magic or ranged is required to fight the Maggot King, as it cannot be attacked with melee until it falls below ~980 hitpoints (65%).

The Maggot King is the most mature and strongest form of the ur-maggot, a parasitic entity that kills its host and later possesses its body. This ur-maggot seems to have killed and then taken over the body of a powerful venator.
summary: The Maggot King is a solo, instanced boss in Vampyrium (east of Sangvesti near the Ruined Village) that requires The Blood Moon Rises and 74 Slayer, assigned as a boss task by Konar, Nieve and Duradel.

strategy: Mammoths are a species of elephant-like creatures that inhabit the area south-east of the Ferox Enclave. They are not very intelligent.

Mammoths can be easily safespotted due to their large size (3x3). Players can use the many trees or tree stumps in the area to safespot them from behind. It is an efficient place to train with a Dwarf multicannon due to the high hitpoints of the Mammoths, a nearby altar providing unlimited Prayer for boosts, and the short walk to the Enclave for resupplying. However, players are vulnerable to player killers while training and are therefore advised not to carry too many supplies on them at once.

strategy: Mogres are Slayer monsters and a type of ogre that are found in Mudskipper Point, requiring level 32 Slayer to kill. Mogres appear when disturbed by the player, who must lure them using Fishing explosives on an Ominous Fishing Spot. Previously, they could only be killed by players who had completed the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest. Since the release of Sailing, Mogres swimming in the ocean can now be killed with cannons from the player's boat. Doing so does not require completion of Skippy and the Mogres and does not demand the use of Fishing explosives, but still requires having level 32 Slayer.

Mogres can only be "lured" by clicking Use on the fishing explosives in your inventory, then clicking on the ominous fishing spots while also standing a few tiles away. Although the ominous fishing spots do have an options to "Lure" or "Bait", both these options do nothing (even with fishing explosives) and instead merely say in chat "Something seems to have scared all the fishes away..."
Mogres are usually killed by players searching for their unique drops of flippers or Mudskipper hats.

Mogres can be safespotted by using the fairy ring, the STASH unit to the west, or along the shoreline. A tinderbox and logs can be brought to make fires, as mogres often drop raw fish. There is also an altar in Rimmington church just to the north of Mudskipper Point to restore prayer if using Protect from Melee.

Since Sailing, swimming mogres in the Ardent Ocean can be killed with a ship cannon without explosives or the miniquest, but 32 Slayer is still required. Bring a tinderbox and logs to cook the raw fish they drop.

strategy: Nechryael are a type of demon that can be assigned as a slayer task at level 80 Slayer and 85 combat by various Slayer masters. They are notable for their frequent drops of herbs, seeds, and alchable items, making them an extremely good slayer task.

Nechryael attack with melee, and can periodically summon up to two death spawns to assist them in battle. These death spawns are fairly inaccurate with a max hit of 2, but as they attack with typeless melee, Protect from Melee has no effect on them. Uniquely, they are able to attack you in single-combat areas regardless of if you are already in combat. It is recommended to bring food if using Melee or to have runes to cast blood spells if using Magic to kill nechryaels. It is also possible to leave the area and return to lose aggression, but this is impractical in most situations.

A stronger variant of the Nechryael, the Greater Nechryael, can be found in the Catacombs of Kourend, Iorwerth Dungeon and Wilderness Slayer Cave. These are mechanically the same as their standard counterparts, barring higher stats. It is highly recommended to kill these whenever possible, as they have a more lucrative drop table. Both variants share the same superior, the Nechryarch, though the common drop table takes from whichever variant they came from. Nechryarch attack with melee, but will periodically summon a trio of chaotic death spawn; one each in melee, magic and ranged. They hit significantly harder, but their attacks can be blocked with prayer. These spawns will only appear if the Nechryarch is allowed to attack the player, so using safespots or farcasting will prevent this from happening.
summary: Nechryael (80 Slayer, 85 combat, Priest in Peril to be assigned) are melee demons that summon up to two death spawns whose typeless hits ignore Protect from Melee and single-combat rules, so bring food or use blood spells. The wiki's fastest option is bursting or barraging the 14 greater nechryael in the Catacombs of Kourend with a goading potion to draw aggression, since they are not aggressive; for melee it recommends the Iorwerth Dungeon (the nechryael there drop crystal shards) with a demonbane weapon such as Emberlight or Arclight. Normal nechryael in the Slayer Tower are safespottable using the tables and buckets, and the Charred Dungeon (60 Sailing) is a multicombat, cannonable spot for normal nechryael. Krystilia tasks must be done in the task-only Wilderness Slayer Cave; bring a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod.

strategy: Otherworldly beings are unusual Zanarian monsters. They are commonly assigned as Slayer tasks by Vannaka. They are found south of the bank in Zanaris and can be safespotted by standing next to the flower pond and attacking the ones on the other side, however they move around quite a lot and players may find them difficult to safespot. An alternate and more consistent safespotting method is standing on the north or south of the pond and corner trapping the mobs on the pond corners.

More specifically, five of the six otherworldly beings have a wander radius which permits safespotting without having them retreat as long as the player stands right next to the pond. One of these five will retreat if attacked horizontally across the pond, and another will retreat when attacked vertically. The other three will not retreat as long as you stay next to the pond.
Otherworldly beings may be a decent source of Magic experience, herbs, runes, and the materials for rings of forging for Ironmen.
summary: Otherworldly beings are level 64 spectral monsters found only south of the bank in Zanaris, assigned by Vannaka at 40 combat after Lost City. They are not aggressive and can be safespotted by standing next to the flower pond and attacking across it, or more reliably by corner-trapping them at the pond corners; they wander a lot, so a couple will retreat if attacked across the pond. They are a decent source of herbs, runes and ring-of-forging materials for ironmen, and an Ectoplasmator gives Prayer XP because they are spectral.
usefulItems: Ranged or Magic for the pond safespot

strategy: The Phantom Muspah is a solo boss that can be fought after completion of the quest Secrets of the North. It is the leftover energy of the Strange Creature that manifested after the events of the quest.

The Phantom Muspah is stronger than its quest variant, but otherwise shares the same attacks and mechanics. All forms of the Phantom Muspah have 33% freeze resistance, meaning it will only stay frozen for 66% of the base freeze duration.

Unique drops from the boss include ancient essence, used in the creation of forgotten brews or upgrading the imbued heart into a saturated heart, and the venator shard, of which five can be combined to create the venator bow, a unique bow that shines in multicombat situations.
summary: The Phantom Muspah is a level 741 solo instanced boss in its lair off the Ghorrock Dungeon beneath Weiss, unlocked by completing Secrets of the North, and can be assigned as a boss task by Konar, Nieve and Duradel.

strategy: Pirates can be assigned as a Slayer task from Krystilia.

Pirates can be found at level 55 Wilderness in the Pirates' Hideout. A lockpick is required to enter. They are combat level 26 and have a very minimal droptable. They are located in single-way combat.

Alternatively, Zombie pirate can be killed. They are combat levels 22, 28, and 34 located at the Chaos Temple. It is located in multi-way combat and a cannon can be used. Nearby Elder Chaos druids will consistently teleblock the player and Protect from Magic is highly recommended. There is a nearby altar to recharge prayer. Zombie pirates have a generous drop table making them a popular monster to kill. It is recommended to complete the medium Wilderness Diary which increases the drop table roll from 15% to 50%.
summary: Pirates are a Krystilia-only Wilderness task (39 Thieving) with two options. The level 26 pirates in the Pirates' Hideout at level 54-55 Wilderness need a lockpick to enter, are in single-way combat and have a minimal drop table. The wiki favours the level 22-34 zombie pirates at the Chaos Temple in level 11 Wilderness, which is multicombat, cannonable and gives a generous drop table (much better with the medium Wilderness diary), but nearby elder chaos druids will teleblock you, so use Protect from Magic and recharge at the temple altar.

strategy: Rats can be assigned as a slayer task from Turael and Spria. They have no requirements to be assigned. There are a wide variety of rats that can count toward the task, but the most commonly killed are rats and giant rats, which are low-level, rarely deal damage, and practically ubiquitous. It is recommended to use Rat bone weapons as it has greatly increased effectiveness against rats.

Scurrius can be fought for greater experience and profit, although his minions will also decrement the task, reducing how many times the boss can be fought on task. Brine rats are accessible during Olaf's Quest, and drop medium clues and the elusive brine sabre.

Hell-rat behemoths can be accessed after Freeing Evil Dave, and drop full spice shakers for spicy stews. Crypt rat and giant crypt rat variations require completion of Priest in Peril for access to Morytania and may be slain by players for the higher Slayer experience reward or for changing their reward potential inside the Barrows minigame.

strategy: Revenants are the ghostly versions of creatures slain during the God Wars found in the Revenant Caves within the Wilderness in levels 19 to 40. They are capable of hitting high and accurately for their combat levels, although most of the damage can be mitigated with a charged bracelet of ethereum. As the Revenant Caves location is members-only, all revenants are members-only creatures.

Revenants have a fairly generous drop table, but as they are in the Wilderness, the player is always at risk of getting killed by other players. Due to the revenants' lucrativeness, player killers are common. The caves they inhabit are singles-plus combat, where PvP situations take priority over PvM: a player in combat with a revenant can be attacked by another player.

Unique drops from the revenants include the Wilderness weapons, a set of weapons that have increased effectiveness against monsters in the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether. They also drop various ancient artefacts, which can be sold to the Emblem Trader wandering within the Revenant Caves for a set amount of coins, as well as ancient crystals, four of which are used to construct an obelisk in the superior garden of a player-owned house.

Revenants are capable of using all three forms of combat. Their attacks have very high accuracy against any player not using a bracelet of ethereum regardless of their defensive bonuses. In addition, their attacks change based on the player's defensive stats and protection prayers being used. They are also capable of healing themselves when their health falls below 50%, though this only occurs a limited amount of times. When it heals itself, a lightning strike can be seen.
Being undead, revenants are susceptible to the effects of the salve amulet and its enchanted version.
summary: A Krystilia-only Wilderness task done in the Revenant Caves, usually with Ranged (Craw's or Webweaver bow) while wearing a charged bracelet of ethereum, which cuts revenant damage by 75% and removes their aggression. Pray Protect from Magic and Protect Item, since magic is their most accurate style. Revenants are undead, so a salve amulet or amulet of avarice boosts damage, and Wilderness weapon drop rates are 5x while on a Krystilia task.

She additionally has a high drop rate of elite clue scrolls for the relative time to defeat her.

Bring a light source and a tinderbox, watch for floor traps and trapdoors, and carry an emergency teleport because the cavern level uses all three styles at once. strategy:
Scorpions can be assigned as a slayer task at level 7 combat by various low end Slayer masters and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. Scorpions attack with melee and a few certain varieties are capable of poisoning. Interestingly various fightable lobsters also counts as scorpions.
Scorpions have very limited drop tables, usually only dropping ensouled scorpion heads and beginner clue scrolls.

Players can also kill Scorpia as part of a scorpion task; however, she is located in extremely deep (50+) Wilderness in a multicombat area, and freezes are required in order to kill the boss efficiently. It is a very popular player killing spot, so players should not bring items they are unwilling to lose.
summary: A beginner task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna (or Krystilia in the Wilderness) done with any combat style against level 14 scorpions, most conveniently in the Al Kharid Mine or the Ardougne Zoo enclosure. Scorpions only melee; a few variants (poison scorpions, Scorpia and her offspring) can poison. Krystilia's version is done west of the Air Obelisk, at the Scorpion Pit or on King Scorpions in the Lava Maze, and a cannon in Scorpia's cave can finish the task in under a minute.

strategy: Shades can be assigned as a slayer task, with no Slayer level requirement by Mazchna and Vannaka. The easiest method to complete this task is by killing Loar Shades in Mort'ton as they are much faster to kill than the level 159/140 Shades found in Stronghold of Security and Catacombs of Kourend respectively.

Shades are susceptible to the Salve Amulet and Crumble Undead (however, their 40% weakness to wind spells means that Wind Bolt will do more damage than Crumble Undead for the same cost of a chaos rune, providing the player has 35 Magic or more). It is worth noting that combat experience gained while fighting the shades in the Stronghold of Security is drastically reduced; the player will gain 1 experience for 10 damage dealt.
summary: Assigned by Mazchna and Vannaka; the fastest way is killing the 25 aggressive level 40 Loar shades around Mort'ton with melee or magic, since they die far quicker than the level 159/140 shades in the Stronghold of Security or Catacombs of Kourend. Shades are undead, so a salve amulet works, and wind spells hit their 40% air weakness; the Stronghold shades give drastically reduced XP and should be avoided.

strategy: Shadow warriors are monsters that can be found in the dungeon beneath the Legends' Guild. They are not considered undead, so the salve amulet has no effect on them, and they are one of few monsters that are hidden on the player's minimap.
After completion of Legends' Quest, shadow warriors are a possible Slayer task from Chaeldar and Vannaka.

Although they do not have the undead or spectral attributes, they are still undead according to the 36th Postbag from the Hedge, as Radimus Erkle says that the shadow warriors are resurrected with necromancy. They also wear spectral plate armour.
It is possible to safespot shadow warriors through the fence separating them from the pit scorpions.
Another spot to use is behind the fungus near the cavern wall. It is still possible to be attacked until the shadow warriors become non-aggressive.
summary: A Vannaka/Chaeldar task after Legends' Quest, done in the dungeon beneath the Legends' Guild where 19 aggressive level 48 shadow warriors spawn. They are melee attackers with high stab defence and low crush and magic defence, so use crush weapons or magic, or safespot them through the fence by the pit scorpions; a cannon can be used in the dungeon. They are not classed as undead, so the salve amulet does nothing.

strategy: The shellbane gryphon is the boss version of gryphons found in a cave in the centre of the Great Conch, requiring level 51 Slayer and completion of Troubled Tortugans to kill. As a Slayer boss, it may only be killed while on a gryphons Slayer task. Gryphon Slayer tasks must be unlocked by purchasing the 'Wings Spread' reward from a Slayer master for 80 Slayer Points in order to be assigned them by Nieve/Steve or Duradel/Kuradal, though this unlock is not required for the shellbane gryphon to be assigned as a boss task from those Slayer masters. Konar can also assign the shellbane gryphon specifically when she assigns a boss task.

The shellbane gryphon can also be killed off-task only if the player has the elite clue step to kill the gryphon. Dropping the elite clue scroll while in the cave will delete the item. Combat Achievements can still be completed when killing the gryphon via this method, though not all are possible due to some requiring several kills without leaving the cave. The gryphon will also not drop anything if the clue is not in your inventory when it dies.
Elder Nama at the cave entrance enforces these rules, and also acts as a scoreboard for the boss, displaying the player's statistics for the fight as well as global statistics.

requiredItems: Elemental shield, Mind shield, Dragonfire shield, Dragonfire ward or Ancient wyvern shield
strategy: Skeletal wyverns are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 72 in order to be harmed. They are found at the end of the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon. There is a shortcut at the ladder to the Ice Dungeon leading to the skeletal wyverns requiring level 82 Agility (or level 77 Agility with a Summer pie). Like other wyverns, they require an elemental shield, mind shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield to reduce damage from their icy breath; however, it is not required to be slain. They are also the only monster that drop granite legs.

Although Tarn in his diary writes that he believes skeletal wyverns are undead, they are actually magically animated remains, different from actual undead creatures. This means that the Salve amulet and its enchanted versions do not work against them. They originate from Fossil Island, having escaped the island via magic. Additionally, their bones radiate a very weak magical aura, and stay colder than room temperature.

Skeletal wyverns are assigned by the Slayer masters Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, and Duradel/Kuradal. Because an elemental shield or better is required to defend against their icy breath, they will only assign them if the player has completed the Elemental Workshop I quest.
summary: A 72 Slayer task from Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve and Duradel done at the end of the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, where an elemental, mind, dragonfire or ancient wyvern shield cuts their icy breath from 50+ to 10. They are draconic, so a dragon hunter lance (pound/swipe) or dragon hunter crossbow is best; pray Protect from Melee in melee range or Protect from Missiles otherwise, and a cannon is allowed in the lower cave. Many players safespot them with a crossbow after they lose aggression, using the cave door or a tile north-west of Steve; a task-only upper area exists but is a no-cannon zone.

strategy: Skeletons are undead monsters that can be assigned as tasks at combat level 15 by various low-level Slayer masters. They are often found in cemeteries and dungeons. A good strategy to kill them is to use melee with a weapon with crush bonuses (such as a Viggora's chainmace) and a salve amulet or salve amulet (e), due to their low crush defence.
Another strategy to kill them would be with magic. Many skeletons have an elemental weakness to earth spells, making those a very effective option.

Players who seek a greater challenge can choose to kill Vet'ion or Calvar'ion. These bosses are significantly stronger than the typical skeleton, but provide plenty of rewards for players who seek to kill them. In order to access Calvar'ion, the player must have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary. Vet'ion only requires completing the Medium Wilderness Diary, but is deeper in the Wilderness and resides in a multicombat area. Accessing the bosses requires a one-time payment of coins, which must be repaid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness. Note that the skeletal hellhounds they summon also count towards the task, so every kill at the boss is equal to five skeletons per spawn.
summary: A beginner task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna (or Krystilia in the Wilderness) against undead skeletons, best killed with a crush weapon and a salve amulet because of their low crush defence, or with earth spells which exploit their elemental weakness. The Edgeville Dungeon has a good cluster that can be cannoned with a quick escape; the Catacombs of Kourend are multicombat with bonus shard and totem drops. Krystilia's version can be done in the Wilderness part of Edgeville Dungeon, the Wilderness mines, or by killing Vet'ion or Calvar'ion.

locations.name: Smoke Devil Dungeon
locations.notes: Only location; 30 smoke devils in the main room and 6 in the boss room, none safespottable. Fairy ring BKP or a ring of dueling to Castle Wars then run south-west. Place the cannon in the centre and stack the devils behind the remains; the cannon is destroyed if set up in the boss room.
requirements: Active smoke devil (or Thermonuclear smoke devil) task

requiredItems: Facemask or Slayer helmet
strategy: Smoke devils can be assigned as a slayer task at level 93 Slayer and level 85 combat by high-end Slayer masters. They are only found in the Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars and can only be fought if on a task. They attack with magical ranged. As with dust devils, players must wear a facemask or slayer helm when fighting smoke devils, or their attacks will always deal moderate damage that also drains stats.
Players may choose between killing smoke devils or their boss variant, the thermonuclear smoke devil.

When killing normal smoke devils, players are highly encouraged to use barrage spells, as smoke devils have a high defence level. Although they have very high magic defence, they have a low magic level, which means most spells will still be reasonably accurate. A cannon is strongly recommended to lure the smoke devils, as their cave is extremely large and trying to stack them without one is significantly slower. Players who have obtained rewards from the elite tier of Combat Achievements should have enough cannonballs for one rotation to lure all the smoke devils, while those without may need to reload their cannon once to do so. Place the cannon in the centre of the dungeon and stack the smoke devils as they aggro, using the remains to the sides to stack them. Restore the stack when three or less smoke devils are left.
summary: A 93 Slayer task done only in the task-only Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars (fairy ring BKP). You must wear a facemask or slayer helmet or their attacks always hit and drain stats; they attack with magical ranged, which Protect from Missiles fully negates. The cave is multicombat, so the usual method is to set a cannon in the centre to lure the devils, stack them behind the piles of remains and barrage them. Players wanting profit can instead kill the Thermonuclear smoke devil boss in its side room.

trainingSummary.cons: Luring smoke devils properly requires a lot of practice and effort.
trainingSummary.pros: Barraging smoke devils currently offers the best experience rates in the game. Drops cover the rune costs.

requiredItems: Reinforced goggles or Slayer helmet
strategy: A sourhog is a boar-like monster introduced in A Porcine of Interest. It requires reinforced goggles to kill, or a Slayer helmet after the quest. If no protection is worn, the caustic saliva they spit will burn the player's eyes, draining the player's current Attack and Defence by 90% and cause 20-30 damage each hit accompanied by the player exclaiming. Sourhogs are aggressive to players regardless of their combat level.

According to Spria, the sourhog was created when two farmers competed in a competition each year, with the same farmer winning each year. The other farmer, who was jealous of his rival, hired a dark wizard to alter one of his pigs, turning it into the Sourhog. This sourhog escaped and successfully bred more of its own kind. Sourhogs prefer to live in underground caves and in primitive tribes.
summary: A Spria-only beginner task fought in the Sourhog Cave just east of Draynor Manor after completing A Porcine of Interest. Wear reinforced goggles or a slayer helmet, otherwise their caustic spit hits 20-30 and drains Attack and Defence by 90%. They are level 37, aggressive regardless of combat level and use crush melee and ranged attacks, and a dwarf multicannon can be used in the cave.

strategy: Spiders can be assigned as a Slayer task by Turael, Spria, and Krystilia. They can be found in numerous places across Gielinor.

Most spiders generally use melee, but a few stronger ones will also use Ranged and/or Magic alongside them. Low-levelled spiders are generally weak to all forms of combat, though higher-levelled spiders are weaker to crush.
There are many varieties of spiders that players can kill as part of a Slayer task, though for low-levels, the spiders around Lumbridge are a reasonable spot.

Most spiders only use melee and are weak to everything, with the stronger ones weaker to crush. Krystilia tasks are usually done at the Wilderness spider hill around level 46 with a cannon, or on the bosses Venenatis or Spindel, and higher-level players can substitute araxytes (92 Slayer) or Sarachnis.

strategy: Spiritual creatures are a potential Slayer assignment given by medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters after completion of Death Plateau, a combat level of 60 and either 60 Strength or Agility with a minimum Slayer level of 63 in order to be assigned them.

There are three types of spiritual creatures players can kill as part of a task: spiritual rangers, the weakest at 63 Slayer, warriors at 68 Slayer, and mages, the only NPCs that drop dragon boots, at 83 Slayer.

These creatures are only found in the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon. As followers of their respective gods, they are aggressive to anyone that is not wearing an item aligned to their god, but will be tolerant otherwise. This is essentially required, as the dungeons are multicombat areas with many monsters, likely resulting in a swift death if this is not met.
summary: Rangers (63 Slayer), warriors (68) and mages (83) found only in the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, both multicombat areas where nothing can be cannoned. Wear an item for each god whose followers you pass (at least Zamorak plus the god you are killing) so the dungeon stays tolerant, or you will be swarmed. The wiki suggests skipping or blocking rangers, killing warriors in Zamorak's Fortress and mages in Armadyl's Eyrie or the Ancient Prison, the latter being where the dragon boots-dropping mages are most concentrated. Many players block this task because it is slow, not AFKable and drops poorly.

trainingSummary.cons: Need to bring energy or stamina potions and restore potions if going to GWD via Trollheim due to chill, unless the Fire of Unseasonal Warmth has been built. Poor experience rates everywhere. Not worth doing for XP unless Slayer points are an issue.
trainingSummary.pros: Mages can give decent profit and have relatively low hitpoints (75 for Zamorak, 85 for Saradomin)

strategy: Suqah can be a good Slayer task, due to the relatively high amount of experience per hour that can be gained from killing them with the help of a dwarf multicannon. However, the use of a dwarf multicannon and toxic blowpipe will also result in a loss of coins due to their lack of valuable drops.
If using the northern area on Lunar Isle, players should pray Protect from Magic and wear armour with high Melee defence, as these Suqah attack with both a melee attack and a magic attack.

Players wishing to avoid the magic damage should fight the suqah on the southern part of the island, such as near the Astral Altar, as these attack with only melee. There are also three melee-only suqah on the south-west part of the island, over the bridge (abutting the city wall); specifically, a cannon can be placed directly north-west of the dead tree to target the melee-only suqah while avoiding the single mage-dealing suqah in the vicinity.
summary: An 85 combat task from Nieve or Duradel done on Lunar Isle after starting Lunar Diplomacy. The northern suqahs are dense and multicombat, so most players cannon them from the safespot by the hill with Ranged while praying Protect from Magic against their Ice Barrage-style attacks; the sparser southern suqahs are melee-only and can be safespotted or meleed in Guthan's with no prayer. Drops are poor, so the wiki suggests blocking the task unless you want AFK experience, and a Seal of Passage is needed to bank unless you have done Dream Mentor or the elite Fremennik diary.

trainingSummary.cons: No notable drops to cover the cost of using the cannon. Requires good defensive armour as well as Protect from Magic since they hit hard with both attack styles.
trainingSummary.pros: Decent experience rates. Relatively fast task when unextended.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Do for XP; skip for profit

strategy: Terror dogs are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 40 (not boostable) to kill. Being the personal pets of Tarn Razorlor, they are first encountered during the miniquest Lair of Tarn Razorlor, in which the player must fight two terror dogs, alongside some animated armour in addition to Tarn himself. Upon completion of the miniquest, more terror dogs can be found in the room.

Terror dogs use an accurate melee attack. As the room they are fought in is a multi-combat area, fighting them can become very dangerous quickly, as multiple terror dogs can attack the player all at once.
Terror dogs do not count toward fulfilling a Slayer task for dogs; they are a separate task. They are the only monsters that drop the Granite helmet.

Players can hide in Tarn's room just north of the terror dogs and wait for them to develop tolerance to the player. This makes combating them significantly less risky. Be sure to log out to check for tolerance, as any dogs aggressive towards the player will remain so until the player exits Tarn's room, even if all other dogs are no longer aggressive. This will also cause all dogs targeting the player to stop and begin wandering around. Players can check to see if the dogs are still aggressive by exiting Tarn's room and waiting at the door for a quick retreat if they are.

It is possible to safespot the dogs from Tarn's room using magic or ranged. The dog must be standing on the tile directly in front of the doorway. Walking back and forth between the bookcases in the room while a dog is following you can help position the dog on the correct tile.

Terror dogs are similar to hellhounds in that they can hit hard and accurately, but have very low Defence. As the only area in which they are found is multi-combat, multiple terror dogs can attack at once. Players should be aware that the room that terror dogs are in at Tarn's Lair will drain prayer at a rate of 1 point per two game ticks, or 50 points per minute (much faster than the Barrows). Players cannot set up a cannon in the room.

Fighting terror dogs (mostly done for Slayer tasks) can be a difficult task for players who are unprepared. They can be safespotted if standing in the recesses after they have became tolerant of players.

High-level players, looking to fill the collection log for the Granite helm, may choose to bring their best ranged gear and a Venator bow to quickly dispatch the Terror dogs. Additionally, a Serpentine helm and Blowpipe can be worn initially to…
summary: A Vannaka-only task at 40 Slayer (not boostable) fought in the multicombat room at the end of Tarn's Lair, reached fastest with a Slayer ring teleport; access needs the Haunted Mine quest. They hit accurately with melee and several can attack at once, so the usual approach is to wait in Tarn's room until they become tolerant, or safespot them from that doorway with Ranged or Magic. Cannons cannot be set up in the lair.
usefulItems: Slayer ring (teleport straight to Tarn's room)

strategy: The Leviathan is a large sea creature found within the Scar, who is encountered during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. Once dwelling in the Eastern Ocean, the Leviathan was inadvertently dragged into the Scar during the Battle for the Eye when Perseriya of the Forgotten Four accidentally opened an abyssal rift in an attempt to teleport reinforcements in.

It has since then adapted to the abyssal environment and has made itself at home in a large lake within the Scar, preying upon those who were unfortunate enough to be pulled into the Scar during the battle. This is seen clearly on accounts of survivors and what remains of the Zarosian fleet in the area.
It is replaced by a stronger variant after completion of the quest which the player can repeatedly fight.

strategy: The thermonuclear smoke devil, often referred to as thermy, is the boss version of the smoke devil. It requires a minimum of 93 Slayer to damage. Located at the Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars, the Thermonuclear smoke devil can only be attacked on a smoke devil task, with the exception of one kill for the Western Provinces Diary (provided that the player has 93 Slayer without boosting).
It is the only monster to drop the smoke battlestaff, jar of smoke, and the pet smoke devil. It drops the occult necklace at a higher rate than smoke devils.
Unlike most NPCs, the Thermonuclear smoke devil is always able to walk through other monsters/players. This is to prevent players from safespotting the boss using the smoke devils found in its lair.

requirements: A leaf-bladed weapon, broad ammunition or Magic Dart

requiredItems: Leaf-bladed weapon (battleaxe, sword or spear), broad arrows, broad or amethyst broad bolts, or Magic Dart (Slayer staff / staff of the dead)
strategy: Turoth can be assigned as a Slayer task from Vannaka, Nieve/Steve, Chaeldar, Konar, or Mortimer, requiring 55 Slayer and 60 combat. They are melee based, and as such Protect from Melee will negate all of their damage. They are only found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon.
Turoth can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows and bolts, or the Magic Dart spell. Attacking with any other weapons or spells will always deal 0 damage.
The superior variant is the spiked turoth; the Bigger and Badder Slayer reward must be unlocked for it to spawn.
Melee:

- Leaf-bladed battleaxe > leaf-bladed sword > leaf-bladed spear
- Decent melee armour (rune or higher, ideally), Slayer helmet or black mask
- Super set, combat potion, or other stat boosting potions
- Nature runes and a fire staff or fire runes to alchemise various drops
- A herb sack
- Method of healing if using weaker armours such as:
- Bones to Peaches
- Food (preferably lobster or better)
- Note: If you happen to run out of food, you can Prayer flick Protect from Melee.
- Note: Remember that you need inventory space for herbs and seeds.
- Note: You can bring the Saradomin godsword or the Ancient mace, although it won't hit, it heals with the damage it would have done.
Ranged:
Use your best crossbow or bow that can fire broad bolts or broad arrows, optionally use amethyst broad bolts for an additional +15 ranged strength.

- Decent ranged armour, Slayer helmet (i) or black mask (i)
- Ranging potion or mix
- Nature runes and a fire staff or fire runes to alchemise various drops
- A herb sack
- Method of healing (if not using the safespot)
- Note: Bones to peaches tablets may prove useful, as they are stackable (healing may prove unnecessary).
Magic:

- Slayer staff or staff of the dead/2000+ casts of Magic Dart
- Decent magic damage boosting armour, Slayer helmet (i) or black mask (i)
- Imbued heart, Magic potion, Magic essence potion, or wizard's mind bombs if desired
- Nature runes and a fire staff or fire runes to alchemise various drops
- A herb sack
- Method of healing (if not using the safespot);
- Note: Safespot is easy to use. Bones to peaches tablets may prove useful, as they are stackable (healing may prove unnecessary).
summary: A 55 Slayer task found only in the seventh chamber of the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (fairy ring AJR or Slayer ring), which can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows or bolts, or Magic Dart. They are melee-only, so Protect from Melee negates all damage, and the rocks on the east wall and the path to the kurask chamber give easy safespots for Ranged or Magic. The area is single-way and cannons cannot be set up in the dungeon; bring a herb sack for their frequent herb and seed drops.
