strategy: TzHaar are an ancient race dwelling underneath the Karamja Volcano in Mor Ul Rek that can be assigned as a Slayer task if the player has unlocked the perk Hot Stuff for 100 slayer points.

TzHaar come in four varieties: the artisans TzHaar-Hur, the sages TzHaar-Mej, hunters TzHaar-Xil, and guards TzHaar-Kets. Killing any of these while wearing a charged ring of wealth increases their chances of dropping gems (and Onyx bolt tips for level 221 TzHaar-Kets).

The Hur and Ket primarily attack with melee, while the Xil can use either melee or ranged, depending on the weapon they are using; those wielding Toktz-xil-ul (resembling a throwing disc) will be able to use both styles, while those wielding Toktz-xil-ak or Toktz-xil-eks use only melee. TzHaar-Mej attack with magic.
styleNotes: TzKal-Zuk: Learner / First cape: First cape
summary: An unlockable task (Hot stuff, 100 Slayer reward points) from Chaeldar, Nieve or Duradel, done in Mor Ul Rek under the Karamja Volcano. Players normally kill TzHaar-Ket or melee-using TzHaar-Xil because they can be safespotted through the vents, while attacking a Hur or Mej draws the surrounding TzHaar onto you. With a fire cape you can enter the inner city and burst or barrage the level 221 Ket near TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges under Protect from Melee; the master may instead offer TzTok-Jad or TzKal-Zuk as the task.

trainingSummary.cons: Barraging requires using blood spells. Completing the Inferno or the Fight Caves quickly requires having expensive equipment.
trainingSummary.pros: Good experience rates when barraging in the inner part of Mor Ul Rek. Drops cover the rune costs. Alternatively, the option to do the Fight Caves on task will be given, or The Inferno if it's already completed. This task can be 'skipped' easily by entering and immediately leaving the Fight Caves, or by dying inside the Fight Caves or The Inferno.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Do if you have access to Blood Barrage/can consistently do Fight Caves. Otherwise, do not unlock.

strategy: Vampyres can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters once the player has completed Priest in Peril and achieved at least level 35 combat. Mostly confined to the Morytania region, access to different variants of vampyres is usually tied to progression within the Myreque questline.
Prior to the Actual Vampyre Slayer unlock, vampyre tasks can only be assigned by Slayer masters Mazchna and Vannaka and only 10 to 20 will be assigned at a time.
Vampyres come in three different attribute tiers which determines their weaknesses to various vampyrebane weapons:
summary: Vampyres are usually done as vyrewatch sentinels in Darkmeyer after Sins of the Father, using melee with a tier 3 vampyrebane weapon (Ivandis flail, blisterwood flail, hallowed flail or sunspear) and Protect from Melee, since sentinels only use melee and are aggressive without a vyre noble disguise. Efaritay's aid stacks with the slayer helmet and is recommended. The Darkmeyer area west of the Arboretum has an altar and bank next to the Drakan's medallion teleport, and sentinels drop the valuable blood shard; after The Blood Moon Rises, venators in Vampyrium are the harder but more lucrative alternative. Low-level tasks (Mazchna or Vannaka, before the Actual Vampyre Slayer unlock) are done on feral vampyres in the Haunted Woods.

trainingSummary.cons: Can only be harmed with the Ivandis flail, Sunspear or blisterwood flail, which results in poor experience rates.
trainingSummary.pros: Killing Vyrewatch Sentinels in Darkmeyer can yield a somewhat decent profit. Does not require supplies, as prayer can be restored at the Statue.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Should not be unlocked for XP. Can be unlocked for profit.

strategy: Venators can be assigned as a Slayer task, exclusively by Mortimer once the player has completed The Blood Moon Rises. Alternatively, after spending 80 Slayer points and unlocking the Actual Vampyre Slayer perk, they can be killed while on a Vampyre task assigned by Konar, Duradel, Nieve, and Chaeldar. Mazchna and Vannaka can also assign Vampyres as a Slayer task by default, though in much lower quantities. Venators can only be found in Vampyrium, in the designated hunting grounds to the south of the entrance portal.

Venators are classified as tier 3 Vampyres, meaning they require the Ivandis flail as a minimum in order to damage them. Other superior weapons, such as blisterwood, the hallowed flail and sunspear will also work. Efaritay's aid is highly recommended for slaying venators, as it provides additional accuracy and damage that stacks on top of the slayer helm, meaning that attacks are much more accurate and stronger compared to using standard rings such as the treasonous or ultor rings. Each Efaritay's aid costs and comes with 200 charges, meaning that each charge costs coins, which is well worth the cost for most players.
summary: Venators are killed with melee using a tier 3 vampyrebane weapon (Ivandis, blisterwood or hallowed flail, sunspear, or blisterwood stakes) in the Apsul or Virer hunting grounds of Vampyrium, which need The Blood Moon Rises completed and 74 Slayer. They melee when adjacent and range otherwise, so pray the matching protection prayer, but turn prayer off during their screech, which damages and drains prayer from anyone using a protection prayer. Efaritay's aid is highly recommended because its accuracy and damage stack with the slayer helmet. Apsul has spawns closer to the altar; Virer has more spawns and is less crowded.

strategy: Venenatis is a large spider that resides in the Silk Chasm, at level 35 Wilderness.
According to Phabelle Bile, Venenatis is the last of her kind, who were hunted to extinction by dwarves.
A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Silk Chasm; if attempted, you will receive the message:

Venenatis attacks with melee towards any player that's adjacent to her, and either magic or ranged for any player out of her melee range. Protection prayers will fully block the attacks, however, they will have their effectiveness reduced for every spiderling alive in the chamber.
Every four attacks, Venenatis will shuffle to another position in her lair. Every two movements will cause her to alternate between ranged and magic attacks.

When a kill starts, Venenatis begins by summoning two spiderlings, who also increase her max hit along with reducing prayer effectiveness. The spiderlings will drain prayer by 1 for every hit made regardless if it damages or not, however they only have 5 health and players will deal their max hit on them regardless of gear. Venenatis can also launch a sticky web that if stood on, damages and drains prayer by 3 and run energy by 10 every few ticks. Venenatis will always alternate between the spiderlings and the sticky web after moving around twice.
If there are more than 10 players in Venenatis' lair, she will move more often and perform a special attack every time she moves, as opposed to every other time.
summary: Venenatis is the Wilderness spider boss in the Silk Chasm, a level 35 Wilderness multi-combat lair south-east of Callisto's Den that needs the medium Wilderness diary or a Venenatis boss task plus a shared 50,000 coin lair fee; Spindel can be killed instead.

strategy: Vet'ion (pronounced ) is a Zamorakian skeletal champion that resides in Vet'ion's Rest, at level 35 Wilderness. Like other bosses in the Wilderness, he can also drop the dragon pickaxe.

Vet'ion has two forms: the (purple) regular form and the (orange) enraged form. After he is defeated in his first form, he will go to his second form, which has a faster attack speed and stronger max hit. After changing forms he will reset any stat reductions applied in the first form. If he is not killed within five minutes in his second form, he will revert to his first form with the same Hitpoints. If he reverts after his hellhounds have been killed, the player(s) will not have to kill them a second time.
According to Andros Mai and as evidenced by the Desecrated Tomb, Vet'ion's power comes from his resting place.

strategy: Vorkath (roughly translated as pathetic failure/weakling/runt in the dragonkin's language) is a draconic boss-monster first encountered during the Dragon Slayer II quest as the penultimate boss. Created by Zorgoth during the Fourth Age's Dragonkin Conflicts, the blue dragon is one of his subjects that has survived his experiments in the laboratory beneath the dragonkin fortress on Ungael. Despite its phenomenal strength, Zorgoth abandoned Vorkath due to its lack of aggression, leaving it as a 'distraction' for any humans that would stumble onto the island.

Vorkath is considered a blue dragon and zombie for the purpose of a Slayer task. As Vorkath is also undead, the Salve amulet and its variants will work on him. However, it does not stack with the Slayer helmet. Vorkath is also immune to recoil damage.
After completing Dragon Slayer II, players may fight Vorkath again, with increased stats and rewards.
summary: Vorkath is the post-Dragon Slayer II dragon boss in the crater on Ungael, reached by Torfinn's boat north of the Rellekka marketplace; the boss task needs 18 Slayer, Dragon Slayer II completed and the 'Like a boss' unlock, and Vorkath also counts as a blue dragon and a zombie for those tasks.

Wall beasts are aggressive holes in the wall; skip the tile in front of a hole to avoid being grabbed. The beast by the entrance respawns if you exit and re-enter.

strategy: Wall beasts can be assigned as a Slayer task by Mazchna at 35 Slayer and 5 Defence in order to equip a Spiny helmet. They are only found in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. As the Spiny helmet (or Slayer helmet) is only required to block their initial attack, players without the Slayer helmet may wish to bring their black mask to swap to afterwards.
summary: Wall beasts are a low-level Mazchna task done in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves with melee. A spiny helmet or slayer helmet must be worn to repel the first grab, after which a black mask can be swapped in. A light source is needed in the caves (a bullseye lantern is safest because open flames can ignite swamp gas), and an antipoison is worth carrying in case a cave slime or cave crawler is attacked. The south-west corner has two spawns close together; killing one respawns the others.
usefulItems: Black mask to swap to after the initial grab

Best cannon spot is in the second large chamber standing against a wall or waste pit. A tortoise safespot behind pillars is about halfway in; terrorbirds can be safespotted through the doors at the entrance with a 9-tile weapon.

strategy: Warped creatures can be assigned as a Slayer task starting at level 56 Slayer by Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, Duradel, and Mortimer. They will only be assigned if the option Warped Reality is purchased, barring Mortimer who will assign them regardless. Warped creatures are found exclusively in the Poison Waste Dungeon, requiring completion of The Path of Glouphrie.
Players must have the crystal chime in their inventory to fight them, otherwise they will be invulnerable.

Warped Tortoises are relatively simple to fight, as they only deal melee damage, which is fully negated by Protect from Melee, although they are weak enough that high crush defence is sufficient to slay them as well. They are available directly at the entrance of the dungeon, making shorter trips viable as banking with the spirit tree is easy. Further into the dungeon, some of the tortoises can be safespotted behind various pillars, so defeating them with Ranged and Magic is also viable.
summary: Warped creatures live only in the Poison Waste Dungeon (partial The Path of Glouphrie, reached via the spirit tree) and are invulnerable unless a crystal chime is in the inventory. Warped tortoises are melee-only, non-aggressive and weak to crush, so they are usually meleed under Protect from Melee at the entrance or safespotted with Ranged or Magic further in; warped terrorbirds are permanently aggressive, attack with melee and ranged, switch styles against your protection prayer, and are best fought wearing earmuffs or a slayer helmet with Protect from Missiles. The whole dungeon is multi-combat and cannonable; the second large chamber with a cannon on the north-western tortoise spawn is the recommended spot for killing both.

trainingSummary.cons: Mediocre experience when not using a cannon. Dungeon is multi-combat and creatures attack with both melee and range.
trainingSummary.pros: Decent experience when using a cannon. Drops cover cost of cannonballs. Food drops and bones to peaches can sustain a high level player.

strategy: Waterfiends can be assigned as a slayer task at 75 combat level by two Slayer masters, Konar and Duradel. Waterfiends can only be assigned as a slayer task after being granted access to the Ancient Cavern. They are found in the Ancient Cavern, Kraken Cove, and Iorwerth Dungeon. Iorwerth Dungeon is only accessible after completing Song of the Elves.

Waterfiends attack with Magic and magical Ranged so protection Prayers cannot be used to negate all of their damage. However, both types of attacks roll against the player's Magic Defence, so armour with Magic Defence bonuses, such as fortified Masori armour, Eclipse moon armour, or Dragonhide armour is most helpful when fighting them. A saturated or imbued heart can also help slightly increase magic defence. Protect from Missiles will be the most helpful if they are dealing too much damage.

Waterfiends have low crush Defence, so crush weapons are recommended, such as an Soulreaper axe (on crush), inquisitor's mace, or abyssal bludgeon. Ranged can also be used in the case of Ranged armour being used to defend against their attacks.
summary: Waterfiends are a rare Konar or Duradel task fought with crush melee (or earth spells, which they are 100% weak to) while wearing magic-defence armour such as dragonhide, since both their magic and magical ranged attacks roll against magic defence and no single prayer blocks everything. Protect from Missiles helps most if damage is high. The Ancient Cavern (games necklace to Barbarian Assault, then the whirlpool) is the usual spot and lets you safespot across the river with Ranged or Magic because their attack range is only 4 tiles; Iorwerth Dungeon has 20 spawns and allows a cannon but needs Song of the Elves. Many players skip the task because the drops are poor.

trainingSummary.cons: Poor experience rates. Requires some attention due to using two different styles at fairly high accuracy. Not worth doing unless Slayer points are an issue.
trainingSummary.pros: Somewhat decent drops.

usefulItems: Crush weapon (inquisitor's mace, abyssal bludgeon, soulreaper axe on crush)

strategy: Werewolves are found in Canifis. They appear as level 24 humans wandering the village until they are attacked, causing them to transform into level 88 werewolves unless the player attacks with Wolfbane, in which case they will remain in human form as long as it is equipped. They will always drop wolf bones, regardless of their form upon death. However, their human and werewolf forms have a separate loot table.

Werewolves do not count towards a regular wolf slayer task. Additionally, it is important to note that they will only count towards a werewolf Slayer task if killed after transforming: killing them in their human form with Wolfbane will not award experience or decrease the slayer task counter.

Werewolves can also be found in the God Wars Dungeon (and Wilderness version). These are slightly stronger than their Canifis variant, and aggressive to those not wearing an item of Zamorak. The werewolf bone for Rag and Bone Man II is not dropped in the God Wars Dungeon, only from the werewolves in Canifis.
There are multiple strategies that can work to reduce damage and speed up the task when killing these for Slayer:

- Players with an Agility level of 40 or higher can set up a dwarf multicannon in the middle of Canifis, then immediately run south-east and begin the Canifis Rooftop Course. This not only allows the cannon to fire at every Werewolf within range as if it were a multicombat area, players can also earn Agility experience and marks of grace while the task completes. As long as the player is on the rooftops, the Werewolves will wander around the area and take damage from the cannon. The cannon will need to be reloaded every other lap or so, depending on course speed and how many Werewolves stay within its range.

- Alternatively, players can set up a dwarf multicannon, run into any nearby building, and close the door. The Werewolves will become aggressive and stack up behind the closed door. Since the player is not actively taking damage, the cannon will target all of them. You will occasionally need to run outside to reload the cannon. This method can be more tedious, as the Werewolves typically stack behind the door in a way that makes it difficult for the cannon to target them. Moving around inside the building should spread them out and alleviate this issue.
- Players using Melee should attack with Wolfbane equipped, preventing the Werewolf's transition to its wolf form. When their health is very low as a human, switch to a different…
summary: Werewolves are a Vannaka-only task done in Canifis, where they walk around as level 24 humans and transform into level 88 werewolves when attacked; kills only count once they have transformed, so do not finish them with Wolfbane equipped. Melee with Protect from Melee is standard, and they can be safespotted over the STASH unit in the village centre or from behind the bar and tables in the pub. A popular method is to set up a cannon in the middle of Canifis and run the rooftop course, or hide inside a building with the door closed so the cannon hits the stacked werewolves. Stronger, aggressive versions exist in the God Wars Dungeon and its Wilderness counterpart.
usefulItems: Wolfbane (optional, to lower incoming damage while in human form)

strategy: Wolves can be assigned as a slayer task at 20 combat level by Turael and Mazchna. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular Wolves only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times.
One fast way to complete a wolves Slayer task is with a Dwarf multicannon in the Stronghold of Security, as it has a large amount of wolves.
summary: Wolves are a Turael, Spria or Mazchna beginner task; regular wolves only bite with fairly accurate melee, so safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on. White Wolf Mountain (multi, cannonable, big wolf on the peak) and Feldip Hills are the main alternatives.

strategy: Wyrms are draconic creatures requiring 62 Slayer to harm. Players can choose to kill any of three different variants for a wyrms task: Wyrms (sometimes referred to as adult wyrms), wyrmlings, and Lava Strykewyrms.
summary: Wyrms (62 Slayer) can be completed on adult wyrms, wyrmlings or lava strykewyrms. Adult wyrms use melee up close and magic from range, so Ranged with Protect from Magic from outside melee distance, or melee with a dragonbane weapon such as the dragon hunter lance, are standard; wyrmlings are melee-only with half the health; lava strykewyrms are aggressive, use melee and ranged and are immune to cannon. The wiki recommends Wyrmscraig (62 Sailing, partial Fallen From Grace) because the surface wyrmling nest is multi-combat, cannonable and beside a bank and the necklace of passage teleport, and the Wyrmscraig Cavern below holds adult wyrms and strykewyrms with a slayer ring teleport. In the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon you need boots of stone, brimstone or granite boots unless the elite Kourend and Kebos diary is done, and cannons cannot be placed in the wyrm area.

strategy: Zombies can be assigned as a slayer task at level 10 combat by various Slayer masters. Zombies are most often found in places that depict death, such as graveyards.
Monkey Zombies, Undead chickens, Undead cows, Undead Druids, Undead ones, Vorkath, Zogres, and Zombie rats can all be killed to satisfy the task. The Zombies Champion does not count towards the task.

Zombies are primarily ignored as they have a very poor drop table, though players who are assigned them have the option of killing Undead Druids or Vorkath, provided they have the requirements to do so.
summary: Zombies are a low-level task (10 Combat) from Turael, Spria, Mazchna and Krystilia that most players finish as fast as possible because ordinary zombies have a very poor drop table. Undead cows and chickens at Alice's farm west of the Ectofuntus are the quickest kills, while Undead Druids in Forthos Dungeon or Vorkath are the profitable alternatives for players with the requirements. On a Krystilia Wilderness task, zombie pirates at the Chaos Temple are lucrative if the Medium Wilderness Diary is done; otherwise the Graveyard of Shadows and eastern Ruins are the Wilderness options. Zombies have a 50 percent elemental weakness to fire spells and use melee.

requiredItems: Fire cape (one-time payment to TzHaar-Ket-Keh to access the Inferno)
strategy: TzKal-Zuk, often referred to as Zuk, is the last monster encountered in the Inferno. It is currently the fourth strongest monster in Old School RuneScape, and the third strongest monster that must be challenged alone.

Zuk can be killed in place of a TzHaar slayer assignment after unlocking the perk Hot Stuff for 100 slayer reward points. Unlike TzTok-Jad, in order to be given the option to be assigned Zuk, the player must have defeated him at least once off-task. Players who defeat Zuk as part of a slayer task will be given 101,890 Slayer experience, and when accounting for the waves and its monsters, around ~125,000 experience in a successful attempt.
summary: TzKal-Zuk is the final monster of the Inferno in Mor Ul Rek and can be chosen in place of a TzHaar slayer task after unlocking Hot Stuff, provided the player has already defeated Zuk once off-task; the Inferno requires a one-time fire cape payment to TzHaar-Ket-Keh.

locations.notes: Travel by Zul-andra teleport scroll or fairy ring BJS and the stepping stones (76 Agility, boostable); board the sacrificial boat at Zul-Andra. Death items are held by Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and are permanently lost on a further unsafe death before reclaiming.
requirements: Like a Boss unlock (200 Slayer reward points)
Regicide completed to the point of reaching Port Tyras
Spoken to High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa to offer yourself as the sacrifice

strategy: Zulrah is a level 725 solo-only snake boss. Before the player can fight Zulrah, players must have completed Regicide to the point of reaching Port Tyras, as well as having spoken with High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa to offer themselves as the sacrifice in place of the gnome child, as Zul-Gwenwynig will prevent the player from boarding the boat until Zul-Harcinqa allows them to be the sacrifice.
Killing Zulrah is a required task for the hard Western Provinces Achievement Diary, which in turn is a requirement for upgrading to the Elite Void set.
summary: Zulrah is a solo-only level 725 snake boss fought at Zulrah's Shrine east of Zul-Andra in the Poison Waste, assigned as a boss task after unlocking Like a Boss and requiring Regicide (to the point of reaching Port Tyras) plus speaking to High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa to be allowed on the sacrificial boat.
usefulItems: Fairy ring BJS with 76 Agility (boostable) for the stepping stones
